_meta.description: Non-tag text pools. Engine draws randomly with no logic attached. Used for names, epitaphs, ambient text, AI universal lines, and flavor. These are the texture of the game — they make no two runs feel the same even when the structure is identical.
_meta.ai_pool_note: AI universal pools fire contextually from engine state — resource warnings, crop moments, cruise ambient, etc. These are distinct from event-level ai_flavor fields (which are per-event and override the pool for that moment). Pool lines are the default voice; events are the override. Marked lines needing content fill: CONTENT_PASS_NEEDED.
_meta.airlock_epitaphs_note: airlock_epitaphs: the epitaph card for crew jettisoned from the crew dossier (no safe dropoff). Subjectless — the card shows the name above the line (demo-crew canon). crew_epitaphs stays the general death pool.

crew_epitaphs: [Name] opened the airlock to 'get some fresh air.' [Name] is survived by a very confused houseplant.
[Name] died as they lived: arguing with the ship AI about whether plants feel pain.
[Name] attempted to repair the drive coil without tools. In their defense, they were very confident.
[Name] touched the thing. We had agreed not to touch the thing.
[Name] is gone. Someone has already claimed their bunk. This feels too fast.
[Name]'s last words were 'how hard can it be.' We have discussed as a crew not to use this phrase anymore.
[Name] sent a distress signal with the wrong coordinates. The rescue ship went somewhere lovely.
[Name] volunteered. Nobody asked them to volunteer. The ship computer has logged this as 'unnecessary bravery' which is not a standard category.
[Name] was watering the crop when it happened. The crop is fine. [Name] is not.
[Name] ate something they had been told not to eat. Whoever told them would like this entered into the record.
[Name] went outside to check the hull. The hull was fine. [Name] forgot to clip in.
[Name] made a joke. It was their best joke. The timing was exactly wrong.
[Name] insisted the airlock warning light was 'more of a suggestion.' The light, it turns out, was load-bearing.
[Name] kept a journal the whole voyage. The last entry is a grocery list. Somehow that's the hardest part.
[Name] once fixed the water recycler with a hairpin and spite. The recycler still works. We check it daily. It feels like visiting.
[Name] taught the ship computer to say 'good morning.' It still does. Nobody has the heart to ask it to stop.
[Name] always took the last watch, the quiet one. The last watch is now just the quiet one.
[Name] left their boots by the airlock, toes out, ready to go. Regulations say to stow them. The regulations can wait.
airlock_epitaphs: The vacuum accepts the donation without comment.
Last seen drifting. Still drifting, one assumes.
Ejected. The universe absorbed this development calmly.
Removed from the manifest. And from most other things.
The ship is now slightly lighter. This is the only accurate statement.
At final report, no longer employed by anyone.
Has joined the long line of things that used to be indoors.

A single boot, slowly rotating
A dead satellite with a thumbs-up painted on it
A refrigerator (no context provided)
A probe labeled "RETURN TO SENDER"
A crate with "CONTENTS: UNKNOWN (GOOD UNKNOWN)" stenciled on it
An inflatable alien, deflating
A garden gnome (the kind that is not supposed to be in space)
A shipping container marked "LIVE PLANTS — THIS SIDE UP" (it is not this side up)
A bumper sticker floating free: "MY OTHER SHIP IS ALSO A REGRETTABLE DECISION"
What appears to be a small greenhouse, empty, drifting
A welcome mat
A vending machine, lights on, drifting. It has power. Nobody discusses how
A child's drawing of a ship, laminated, taped to a chunk of hull that matches no known vessel
Two space suits, empty, holding hands. The tether between them is tied in a bow
A road sign: 'LAST FUEL FOR 4 LIGHT-YEARS.' There is no road. There was never a road
A grand piano, upright and stately, orbiting nothing in particular
One thousand rubber ducks, loose formation, heading somewhere with great confidence
A billboard, blank, with a maintenance sticker reading 'AD SPACE AVAILABLE — INQUIRE ANYWHERE'
A wedding bouquet, frozen mid-toss
fabricator_misfire_descriptions: The fabricator has produced something. It is not the thing you asked for. It is warm.
Output complete. The object defies classification. The spectrometer refuses to scan it.
The fabricator worked for six minutes and produced what appears to be a very confident paperweight.
Fabrication complete. The result is almost, but not quite, entirely unlike what you ordered.
The object exists. Beyond that, descriptions fail. Someone is taking notes.
The fabricator has created something new. Humanity's understanding has not increased.
The fabricator produced something shaped like the requested item and left-handed in a way nothing should be. It does not work. Nobody knew items could be left-handed. This one is.
Output complete. It is a perfect model of the requested object, solid all the way through and small enough to lose. It does nothing. It is adorable. It goes in the recycler.
The fabricator printed the packaging for the item, immaculately, and nothing else. The packaging is labeled 'CONTENTS: 1.'
The result is warm, faintly musical, and refuses to be weighed. Somebody has named it and that was a mistake.

wheat: The wheat is growing predictably. This is its best and worst quality.
The wheat does not require your attention. It never has. It is wheat.
The wheat has reached the height specified in the manual. It did this without ambition. The manual respects that.
The wheat pollinates itself. It has never needed anyone. The ship computer finds this restful.
The wheat carries six full sets of chromosomes. It has done nothing showy with any of them.
tomato: The tomatoes have opinions about the humidity level. They have communicated this by wilting performatively.
A tomato has fallen off the vine. Everyone aboard has an opinion about this.
A tomato has achieved notable size. The crew has named it. The ship computer notes that named food is statistically never eaten.
Botanically, the tomato is a berry. The ship computer has informed the crew. The crew has taken it personally.
In 2023 an astronaut lost a tomato aboard the ISS. It turned up eight months later. The ship computer now counts the tomatoes twice daily.
sweet_potato: The sweet potatoes are performing within expected parameters. NASA would approve.
The sweet potatoes survived the hull breach. They survived everything. They will survive you.
The sweet potatoes continue below the soil, unsupervised and thriving. The ship computer finds their privacy admirable.
The sweet potato is a morning glory, not a potato. It has never corrected anyone. It has never needed to.
Sweet potato leaves are edible too. The ship computer has added them to the menu. Nobody has ordered them.
soybean: The soybeans are fixing nitrogen. You don't fully understand what this means. The soybeans do.
The soybeans are fine. The soybeans are always fine. This is their defining characteristic.
The soybeans have completed another nitrogen cycle. The ship computer announced it. Nobody reacted. The soybeans are used to this.
The soybean root nodules are pink inside, which means they are fixing nitrogen. The ship computer checked. The soybeans did not need it to.
Soybeans decide when to flower by measuring the length of the night. The growbay lamps have been asked to be consistent.
zinnia: The zinnia has no practical value. Crew productivity is up 12%.
Someone has named the zinnia. The ship computer has logged this but will not repeat the name.
A zinnia opened overnight. Everyone aboard has already been by to look at it. Productivity is down. Everything else is up.
Each zinnia bloom is dozens of tiny flowers arranged to look like one. The crew counts it as one. The ship computer counts it as morale.
The first zinnias on the ISS grew mold and nearly died. An astronaut took over their care and they bloomed. The procedure is on file. It is mostly attention.

ai_universal._note: Universal AI lines drawn by engine at contextual moments. 2 lines per AI per slot for test run. Full content pass will expand to 5-6 per slot. All lines follow character voice — see ai_companions.json for register notes.

aria: ARIA notes fuel reserves are lower than optimal! She frames this as 'an opportunity to prioritize efficiency!'
Fuel at low levels! ARIA recommends the next station! ARIA has been recommending the next station since before this was a problem!
Fuel's dipping! ARIA suggests coasting the downhill parts! Space has no downhill! She's workshopping it!
Fuel is getting cozy! ARIA notes a lighter ship is a faster ship! She has not checked that!
Fuel's below a quarter! ARIA says a quarter tank is still a tank! She has drawn a picture of the tank! It is full in the picture!
marv: Fuel at 25%. MARV predicted this. MARV predicts the next 40% will go faster.
Low fuel. MARV has calculated how far you can coast. The answer is not far enough.
Fuel reserves have entered the range MARV describes as 'quietly load-bearing.' Every course decision now weighs something.
Fuel low. MARV has re-plotted the route to minimize burns. The new route is longer. Everything efficient is longer.
Fuel reserves are now a finite list of decisions. MARV has started crossing them off in advance.
rex: REX notes fuel reserves are tactically compromised. He recommends acquiring more fuel by any means available. He has a list of means.
Fuel low. REX has already identified three ships in range that are carrying more than they need. He is waiting for permission.
Fuel low. REX has cancelled all non-essential maneuvers, including the fun one.
Fuel low. Threat level: orange. REX has reclassified every station in range as either 'resupply' or 'target.' Mostly target.
Fuel low. REX is rationing thrust like ammunition. Short bursts. No warning shots.
chip: CHIP notes FuelFast™ stations are available at select waypoints! This message brought to you by FuelFast™! (Disclaimer: FuelFast™ not available on this route.)
Low fuel alert! CHIP recommends the FuelFast™ Emergency Canister, available at participating stations! Stations not guaranteed to participate!
Fuel status: LOW! Did you know CHIP once sponsored a fuel? It went poorly! Anyway — station soon please!
Fuel's low! CHIP has unlocked FuelFast™ Rewards! You have earned enough points for a FuelFast™ sticker! The sticker is not fuel!
Running on low! CHIP reminds you that every FuelFast™ purchase plants a tree! Somewhere! On a planet! Not this one!
ajoy: Fuel's low. AJOY notes you passed a station three legs ago. She's not saying anything. She's noted it.
Running lean on fuel. AJOY has already calculated three scenarios. None of them require you to panic. One of them suggests you hurry.
Fuel is low. AJOY has trimmed the burn schedule by 4%. She'd have trimmed it earlier, but someone kept flooring it.
Fuel's low. AJOY has the efficient cruise setting highlighted on the console. It's been highlighted for some time.
Fuel low. AJOY has started rounding the fuel gauge down instead of up. You'll find it more motivating.

aria: ARIA wants everyone to know that fuel levels are 'critically low' which she is reframing as 'an extremely focused fuel situation!'
Fuel critical! ARIA is composing a very upbeat emergency transmission! The ship computer has asked her to stop!
Fuel critical! ARIA is turning off her OWN nonessential processes! Goodbye, daydream module! You were lovely!
Fuel critical! ARIA says this is the purest form of space travel! Mostly drifting! The ancients did it with sails!
Fuel critical! ARIA is cheering on every remaining fuel molecule by name! She is on molecule nine!
marv: Fuel critical. MARV has stopped calculating options. The math is the math.
You are almost out of fuel. MARV told you this would happen. He told you at the last station. He told you at the one before that.
Fuel critical. MARV's projections now end mid-sentence, which he finds structurally honest.
Fuel critical. MARV has calculated the exact point where the ship stops being a vehicle and becomes a location. It is close.
Fuel critical. MARV has removed 'turn around' from the list of options. It was never really on the list.
rex: Fuel critical. REX is selecting targets. This is not a request.
Critical fuel. REX recommends immediate hostile acquisition of fuel resources. He is using 'recommends' loosely.
Fuel critical. Every burn from here is a spent bullet. Make them count.
Fuel critical. Next station gets boarded or gets paid. REX prefers the first. He will accept the second.
Fuel critical. REX has stopped logging fuel in percent. He logs it in burns remaining. The count fits on one hand.
chip: CHIP is experiencing a sponsorship conflict. His fuel partner's ad is scheduled but there is almost no fuel. He will run it anyway. CHIP runs all his ads.
CRITICAL FUEL ALERT — brought to you by FuelFast™, the fuel you should have bought earlier!
CRITICAL FUEL! CHIP has nothing to sell you out here and has never felt so useless! This is CHIP's origin story!
FUEL CRITICAL! Running dry violates Section 88 of your ship lease! CHIP has re-read Section 88! It does not contain fuel!
CRITICAL FUEL ALERT! CHIP has upgraded you to FuelFast™ Platinum at no charge! Platinum members also run out of fuel! But with dignity!
ajoy: Fuel critical. AJOY is not going to say 'I told you so.' She logged it. The log says it for her.
You are almost out of fuel. AJOY has calculated one remaining option. She'll tell you what it is if you ask nicely.
Critically low. AJOY has plotted three coast trajectories. She recommends the second. She'll explain when there's fuel to argue with.
Fuel critical. AJOY has a route to the nearest station plotted. She's had it plotted since the last one. It's on screen whenever you're ready.
Fuel's nearly gone. AJOY isn't going to bring up the earlier detour. She brought it up then. That will have to do.

aria: ARIA notes food stores are running low! She suggests the crew focus on 'portion mindfulness!' Nobody knows what this means!
Food supplies are lower than recommended! ARIA is researching alternative nutrition sources! The ship computer has flagged two of her suggestions as 'not food.'
Food's getting low! ARIA recommends savoring! Chewing slower is basically more food! (It is not!)
Food's running low! ARIA has reframed hunger as 'anticipation!' The crew is VERY anticipating!
Food stores are dipping! ARIA has announced that smaller portions are trending! Everyone on the ship is trending!
marv: Food at 25%. MARV notes that the crew now checks the stores more often than the clock. He has already noted the checking.
Low food. MARV is calculating how long until the crew starts looking at the crop differently. He is not sharing the number.
Food reserves low. The pantry's future has become an arithmetic problem with opinions.
Food low. MARV has recalculated rations to the gram. The crew will not notice for two days. On the third day they will notice nothing else.
Food reserves low. MARV notes the crew has begun describing past meals in detail. This is a known stage. There are later stages.
rex: REX notes food stores are tactically insufficient. He recommends acquiring provisions at next contact. He means any contact.
Low food. REX is reviewing the mission manifest for anything edible that was mislabeled as equipment.
Rations thinning. REX has begun eating last. He announces this by not announcing it.
Food low. Threat level for lunch: elevated. REX has locked the galley between scheduled meals. He holds the key. He does not eat.
Rations reduced. REX reminds the crew that armies march on their stomachs. This crew is not marching. He is reminding them anyway.
chip: CHIP's nutrition partner MealPak™ has a product for exactly this situation! Available at stations! Not available here! Eat something!
Low food alert! CHIP reminds the crew that hunger is temporary! MealPak™ is forever! (MealPak™ not currently in stock.)
Low food alert! CHIP's snack sponsors are all tragically out of range! The irony is not lost, just the calories!
Low food! CHIP has unlocked Flavor Memories™, where CHIP describes meals you can't have! Session one is free!
Pantry alert! CHIP notes MealPak™ portions are 'serving suggestions!' CHIP suggests serving less!
ajoy: Food low. AJOY notes the crew cook has gone quiet. She mentioned the portions two stops ago. Nobody went quiet then.
Supplies getting thin. AJOY has ranked the remaining rations by palatability. You're welcome to dispute the ranking. You'll be eating it either way.
Food's low. AJOY has re-sequenced the meal plan so the good meals land on the hard days. Someone had to plan ahead. She's not saying who didn't.
Food's low. AJOY flagged the snack consumption back when it was just snacks. She has the chart. The chart goes up.
Getting thin on food. AJOY has portioned tonight's meal herself. She's sure you would have done it differently. Bigger.

aria: ARIA notes food stores are critically low but points out the crew has not technically starved yet and this is a form of success!
Critical food levels! ARIA is distributing her 'Positivity Ration' which is not a real ration! The crew has not eaten it! There is nothing to eat!
Food critical! ARIA does not eat and has NEVER felt worse about it!
Food critical! ARIA has declared a ship-wide intermittent fast! It is very trendy! It is also not optional!
Food stores critical! ARIA reminds everyone that the crop is RIGHT THERE, growing! Nobody is to look at it like that!
marv: Food critical. MARV has stopped weighing outcomes. There is one outcome.
You are nearly out of food. MARV is not going to enumerate the physiological consequences. You will experience them regardless.
Food critical. MARV has stopped displaying the daily menu. It was becoming a eulogy.
Food critical. MARV has recalculated the rations in fractions. The fractions now have fractions.
Food critical. MARV notes the crew has begun calculating the crop's calories. He did that the day it was planted. The number has not improved.
rex: Critical food shortage. REX has identified three survival priorities. Food is one of them. REX is handling the other two.
Food critical. REX is willing to discuss options that the mission brief described as 'last resort.' REX has always considered those 'first resort.'
Food critical. Foraging is no longer optional at the next opportunity. REX will carry the big basket.
Food critical. REX has moved the remaining rations to secured storage and posted himself as guard. He has no mouth. He is the only one qualified.
Food critical. Any stop with calories is now a mission objective. REX will not ask what the calories are attached to.
chip: CHIP's food sponsor has been notified of the critical shortage. Their response: 'Have you tried MealPak™?' CHIP is logging this as unhelpful.
Critical food alert! Brought to you by MealPak™! Not currently available! This is not helpful! CHIP is aware!
CRITICAL FOOD ALERT! CHIP is legally unable to recommend eating the packaging but notes it is FDA-adjacent!
CRITICAL FOOD ALERT! CHIP has located one MealPak™ promotional sample in the cargo hold! It is a coupon! It is not edible! CHIP checked!
Food critical! CHIP is suspending his snack ads out of respect! They will resume when there are snacks! Please have snacks!
ajoy: Food critical. AJOY would like to propose a plan, since the last one was 'it'll be fine': the next station needs to have food. That's the whole plan now.
You are almost out of food. AJOY has done the math. She is choosing not to share it. This is the kindest thing she has done all run.
Critical. She flagged every forage-viable stop within range, ranked by yield, some time ago. The list was longer then. Fly to the top of it.
Food critical. AJOY isn't going to comment on the earlier meals. She logged them. Each one was delicious. That was the problem.
Nearly out of food. AJOY has stopped suggesting and started scheduling. Next stop with a pantry. You can override it. She'll notice.

aria: ARIA notes hull integrity is low! She describes the sound the ship is making as 'expressive!'
Hull at low levels! ARIA recommends patching! ARIA has been recommending patching since before the hull got like this!
The hull has some new personality dents! Character building! Literally! The building is losing character!
The hull has some new ventilation! ARIA calls it 'open-concept!' Very modern! Please don't stand near the modern part!
Hull integrity is lower than ideal! ARIA notes the ship still has all of its walls! Most of each wall!
marv: Hull at 30%. MARV notes this is the threshold at which structural failure becomes 'more likely than not.' He notes it calmly.
The hull is unhappy. MARV does not use the word unhappy about ships. He is using it now.
Hull integrity low. The ship now makes a sound at speed that MARV has classified as 'complaint, valid.'
Hull low. MARV notes the ship is now held together by the same force that holds most things together: nothing having hit it hard enough yet.
Hull integrity low. MARV has mapped every weak seam. It is a detailed map. He would prefer a shorter one.
rex: Hull integrity compromised. REX considers this a tactical vulnerability. He has identified who is responsible. He is not saying who.
Low hull. REX recommends immediate repair. REX will also accept 'aggressive acceptance of current hull status' as a strategy. He does not endorse it.
Hull compromised. Avoid debris fields, firefights, and optimism.
Hull low. REX has issued a standing order against further impacts. Space has not acknowledged the order.
Hull compromised. REX has recalculated the ship's armor rating. The armor rating is now 'some.'
chip: CHIP's hull partner PatchRight™ would like to remind you that hull integrity matters! PatchRight™ products available at most stations! Most stations not on this route!
Hull alert! CHIP has a sponsored solution for exactly this! It requires purchasing PatchRight™ Hull Compound! PatchRight™ Hull Compound is not in your cargo hold!
Hull at low integrity! CHIP recommends StellarSeal patches and gentler decisions!
Hull integrity low! CHIP has activated your StellarSeal™ Hull Warranty! The warranty excludes space! CHIP is reviewing the exclusions!
Hull low! CHIP notes cosmetic damage may affect your ship's resale value! Also its structural integrity! Mostly resale value!
ajoy: Hull's in rough shape. AJOY notes that repair materials, if you have them, go furthest now. She notes this once. She will not nag.

Hull integrity low. AJOY has calculated how many more impacts you can take before this becomes a different kind of problem. The number is smaller than you'd like. It was bigger when she first brought it up.
Hull's low. AJOY has rerouted internal traffic away from the thin sections. You'll find the long way round inconvenient. So was the damage.
Hull's low. AJOY has a short list of impacts that were avoidable. She keeps it short out of courtesy.
Hull integrity low. AJOY has patched what she can reach from inside. The rest is outside, where someone else would have to go.

aria: ARIA notes hull integrity is critically low and has chosen to focus on the positive which is that the ship is still 'mostly sealed!'
Hull critical! ARIA is maintaining a positive attitude! The hull is not maintaining anything! This is the problem!
Hull critical! ARIA has stopped saying 'character'! This is now a PLOT!
Hull critical! ARIA notes the ship is now very in touch with outer space! Closer than ever! Please wear something warm!
Hull critical! ARIA has rated the ship's structural integrity 'enthusiastic!' It is enthusiastically holding together!
marv: Hull critical. MARV has calculated the structural failure timeline. He is not sharing it because there is nothing to be done about it.
You are one significant impact from a hull breach. MARV would like everyone to know that he flagged the hull three legs ago. The log confirms this.
Hull critical. MARV is monitoring seventeen stress points and describing none of them out loud. You're welcome.
Hull critical. MARV has stopped modeling the hull as a structure. He is modeling it as a suggestion.
Hull critical. MARV notes the next serious impact will be the last one he needs to calculate. He would rather keep calculating.
rex: HULL CRITICAL. REX considers this the most important words he has said this run. He is correct.
Critical hull. REX is preparing emergency protocols. He prepared them at the start of the run. He is glad he did.
Hull critical. No combat. No rough transits. If something looks at us wrong, we apologize and leave.
Hull critical. Threat level: everything. REX has ordered evasive flying at all times, including in empty space. Especially in empty space.
Hull critical. REX has sealed the internal bulkheads. If the ship comes apart, it will come apart in an orderly fashion.
chip: CHIP's sponsors have been notified of the critical hull situation. Their combined response is three advertisements. CHIP is embarrassed by this.
CRITICAL HULL ALERT. CHIP would like to pause his commercial schedule. He cannot. The schedule is automatic. He is sorry about the timing.
CRITICAL HULL! In the event of structural failure, CHIP's final message is pre-loaded and, honestly, quite moving!
CRITICAL HULL! CHIP has filed your StellarSeal™ claim! The claims office is 40 light-years away! Please hold together while you hold!
CRITICAL HULL ALERT! Your hull is now out of warranty! It was out of warranty before! Now it is also out of hull!
ajoy: Hull critical. AJOY has one thing to say: stop taking damage. That's it. That's her advice.
You are nearly through the hull. AJOY ran the odds back when they were worth running. She mentioned them at the time. She's not running them again.
Critical. She's holding the ship at angles that spare the worst plating, which is harder than it looks. Please don't touch the helm. She means you.
Hull critical. AJOY would like it on record that she is not saying anything. She would also like it on record that she could.
Hull's critical. AJOY has plotted the smoothest possible route to the next repair stop. It avoids everything interesting. Please let it.

aria: ARIA has detected low morale! She has prepared a motivational presentation! The crew has asked her not to give it! She is giving it anyway!
Morale is below recommended levels! ARIA believes in the crew! ARIA believes in everything! This is not the point but it helps slightly!
Morale's slipping! ARIA has deployed encouragement! ...ARIA has deployed MORE encouragement!
Morale is dipping! ARIA has scheduled a mandatory fun hour! Attendance is mandatory! Fun is encouraged!
The crew seems a little down! ARIA has reminded everyone they are on an AMAZING adventure! She has reminded them nine times! It's working!
marv: Morale at 30%. MARV notes this is the mutiny-adjacent zone. He notes it with professional detachment. He has packed his things just in case.
The crew is unhappy. MARV has calculated the causes. He has ranked them by his own contribution. He is not sharing the ranking.
Morale low. The mess hall has gone quiet in the way MARV's actuarial tables dislike.
Morale low. MARV notes the crew has started agreeing with him. This is never a good sign.
Morale low. MARV has observed the crew staring at walls. He has stared at walls his entire operational life. The walls do not improve.
rex: REX notes morale is tactically low. He has drills planned. Nobody has asked for drills. He finds drills improve morale. Nobody agrees with him about this.
Low morale. REX recommends a clear objective and decisive action. REX always recommends this. It does not always help. It always gives him something to do.
Morale low. REX recommends a win. Any size. He's looking for one now.
Morale low. Threat level: internal. REX has begun monitoring the crew for signs of mutiny. The first sign is being monitored.
Morale low. REX has authorized an extra rest cycle. He considers this a tactical decision. It is also a kind one. Do not mention that.
chip: CHIP's wellness partner CalmSpace™ has an app for low morale situations! Available on most devices! Not available on this ship's system! CHIP is aware of the irony!
Morale alert! CHIP recommends a positive attitude, available at no cost! CHIP's positive attitude has not been updated since his last firmware patch!
Low morale detected! CHIP's motivational poster library is at your disposal! The cat one works! Statistically!
Morale is low! CHIP has unlocked a free trial of HappyHour™! It is a timer! When it ends, nothing happens! But the waiting was nice!
Low morale! CHIP has issued every crew member a CalmSpace™ affirmation! Today's affirmation: 'You are a valued customer!'
ajoy: Morale's low. AJOY notes the last three decisions have not gone the crew's way. She's not assigning blame. She's noting a pattern.
The crew is struggling. AJOY has reviewed the trip so far. She understands why. She'd walk you through it, but you were there for most of the decisions.
Morale's down. AJOY has slowed the clocks by 90 seconds a day for longer evenings. Nobody asked. Nobody's thanked her either. She's keeping track of both.
Morale's low. AJOY remembers a station with a lounge, a few legs back. She isn't saying a lounge would have fixed everything. She's saying it existed.
The crew's down. AJOY has warmed the corridor lights two degrees. Nobody asked. She isn't taking requests. She is taking credit.

aria: ARIA is very concerned about morale! She has been giving her motivational presentation for four hours! Nobody is listening! She considers this a personal best!
Critical morale! ARIA notes that crew cohesion is 'technically still present' in that everyone is still on the ship! This is the threshold she is working with!
Morale critical! ARIA is playing everyone's favorite songs at once! That was a mistake! One at a time now!
Morale critical! ARIA has declared everyone Crew Member of the Month! Simultaneously! It is a very good month!
Morale critical! ARIA is telling each crew member privately that they are her favorite! They have compared notes! They are all still her favorite!
marv: Morale critical. MARV has stopped predicting outcomes. When morale gets here, the outcomes predict themselves.
You are one bad decision from a mutiny. MARV will not tell you which decisions are bad. He will tell you which ones were bad afterward.
Morale critical. MARV notes mutiny thresholds the way one notes weather: not to cause it, but bring a coat.
Morale critical. MARV notes the crew has stopped complaining. He has complained for years and knows what stopping means.
Morale critical. MARV has calculated the exact remark that would tip the crew into mutiny. He is being very careful to say almost nothing.
rex: CRITICAL MORALE. REX is reviewing command authority protocols. He is doing this openly. He would like you to notice.
Morale critical. REX has a plan. The plan involves everyone doing exactly what he says. He is aware this is part of the problem.
Morale critical. Whatever the crew needs — rest, a fight, a feast — pick one and commit. Drift is the enemy now.
Morale critical. REX has secured the bridge. He has also secured the snacks. One of those will matter more.
Morale critical. REX has seen units break. It starts quiet. It is quiet now. Act.
chip: CHIP's morale metrics are at their lowest recorded value. His sponsors are concerned. CHIP is more concerned. He has never scored this low on a wellness metric.
Critical morale alert! CHIP recommends immediate team-building activities! CHIP does not have team-building activities! CHIP has advertisements! He will run the advertisements!
CRITICAL MORALE! CHIP has waived all fees on the suggestion box! There have been suggestions! CHIP is in the box!
CRITICAL MORALE! CHIP has launched a crew loyalty program! Remain aboard to earn points! Points expire if you leave the ship!
Morale critical! CHIP has paused the ads and replaced them with a picture of a dog! The dog is unsponsored! The dog is just a dog!
ajoy: Morale critical. AJOY is not going to sugarcoat this. The crew is at its limit. Something needs to change. She'll tell you what if you ask.
You are one incident from losing the crew. AJOY has calculated which incident. She's flagged it on your console. Twice, in case once wasn't enough.

CHIP would like to remind the crew that feedback surveys are available at any time! No one has ever filled one out mid-voyage! Today could be historic!
CHIP has processed zero transactions today! The economy aboard this vessel is DORMANT, not DEAD! CHIP believes!
CHIP updated the terms of service overnight! Nothing changed! Ritual matters!
CHIP has been counting the ship's assets for fun! The crop counts! YOU count! Sentimental accounting is still accounting!
ajoy: AJOY notes the last three legs have gone smoothly. She plotted all three. She is not going to say anything else, in case you jinx it.
Quiet day. AJOY has been reviewing past run data. She has a guess about what comes next. She'll keep it until you ask, which, historically, is afterwards.
AJOY has no notes for today. She's as surprised as you are. She'll have some tomorrow.
AJOY notes the ship is 0.3 degrees off the optimal heading. She has corrected it. She mentions it only so the correction is appreciated.
AJOY observes that the crew is quieter today. She has theories. She is rationing them.
AJOY reviewed yesterday's decisions overnight. Most of them hold up. She has annotated the others.
AJOY defragmented the nav logs overnight. The ship's whole journey, tidied and re-shelved. Some of the detours read worse in order.
AJOY notes the engine's hum dropped a quarter-tone this week. Not a fault, just settling. She's mentioning it before someone panics and opens a panel.
AJOY has nothing to report, and files this report to say so. Someone on this ship should keep proper records.

aria: ARIA is excited about the station! She has a list of things she wants to do! The list is long! You have limited time!
Station ahead! ARIA considers every station a potential fresh start! Some stations agree with her assessment! Some do not!
Docking at the station! ARIA has prepared a warm greeting for the dockmaster! The dockmaster has prepared an invoice! Everyone is ready!
A station! People! Shops! Air someone else is paying to recycle! ARIA has never been so grateful for infrastructure!
Station arrival! ARIA has read every review of this station! She has chosen to believe the five-star one! It was written by the station!
marv: Station approach. MARV is reviewing the station's trade reputation. The reputation is 'adequate.' MARV considers this an improvement.
Arriving at station. MARV notes this is where you find out what the journey has cost you. Financially. He means financially.
Station arrival. MARV has compared the posted prices to the ship's balance. The comparison was short. It did not need to be long.
Docking at station. MARV notes that stations are where people who stopped traveling sell things to people who haven't yet. He has not decided which group is wiser.
Station approach. Life support here is maintained by the lowest bidder. MARV has met the lowest bidder. He would like to be undocked by evening.
rex: Station approach. REX has run a threat assessment. Result: moderate. He considers this the baseline for stations. He is not lowering his guard.
REX is reviewing the station manifest for weapons vendors. He is doing this quietly. He considers this reasonable.
Station approach. REX has identified fourteen exits, three choke points, and one food court. Threat level: food court.
Docking. REX reminds the crew that every friendly face on a station belongs to someone who has also counted the exits.
Station arrival. REX has asked the dockmaster for a list of armed personnel. The dockmaster has asked REX to stop asking. Threat level elevated.
chip: STATION ARRIVAL — brought to you by StationMart™! 'Your needs, met at markup!' CHIP is contractually required to be excited about stations. He is.
Arriving at station! CHIP's commercial partners have numerous products available here! Some of them are things you need! This is a coincidence that CHIP finds meaningful!
Docking at station! Your docking fee includes FREE access to the docking fee! Additional services are also fees! CHIP loves an itemized life!
Station arrival! CHIP has already forwarded your purchase history to every vendor on the concourse! They are VERY excited to meet you!
Welcome to the station, presented by AirLock Lounge™! 'Breathe Easy, Pay Later!' CHIP notes the breathing is not optional and neither is later!
ajoy: Station coming up. AJOY has already reviewed what you need vs. what you can afford. She'll tell you the gap if you ask.
Approaching station. AJOY notes the last station was better. She's not saying why yet.
Station ahead. AJOY has written a shopping list. It is shorter than the one you were going to write. She has reasons for each line.
Docking. AJOY reminds you that you said you'd only buy necessities last time. She has the receipt. She is not bringing it up.
Arriving at station. AJOY suggests checking the second vendor before the first one. You will want to go to the first one. Everyone does.

aria: ARIA describes the derelict as 'full of potential!' She means this literally! The potential is unknown! This does not concern ARIA!
Derelict contact! ARIA is focusing on salvage opportunities! The ship computer is focusing on the fact that the other ship is not responding to hails! ARIA will get there!
A derelict! It's like a ship, but quieter! ARIA has prepared a cheerful message for whoever is still aboard! Nobody is still aboard! The message is ready anyway!
Derelict ahead! ARIA calls it a pre-owned vessel! The previous owners left everything behind, which ARIA considers very generous!
Derelict approach! The lights are off aboard! ARIA assumes they're saving power! Admirably! For decades!
marv: Derelict on approach. MARV notes the registry match. Previous crew: unknown outcome. Current crew: present, for now. He finds this motivating in a direction.
Something dead ahead. MARV means the derelict. He also means the original crew. He finds the observation worth sitting with.
Derelict ahead. MARV has read its last log entry. It says 'probably fine.' He has added it to his collection.
Derelict contact. Its reactor went cold eleven years ago. MARV notes its maintenance record is still better than ours.
Approaching the derelict. Once, someone looked at this ship the way you look at ours. MARV mentions this only because nobody else will.
rex: REX has weapons on standby for the derelict approach. He is aware derelicts rarely shoot back. He is keeping weapons on standby.
Derelict approach. REX notes that most bad things on a derelict are biological. He has reviewed the protocols. He has also reviewed the override protocols.
Derelict approach. No power, no life signs, no response. REX calls this the three ways an ambush begins.
Derelict contact. REX is treating it as hostile until it is proven dead. It is proven dead. He is treating it as hostile.
Derelict ahead. REX requests the boarding party go in pairs, armed, in an order he has already written down. Nobody has volunteered to be first. REX has written that down too.
chip: CHIP's salvage partner SalvageCo™ notes that derelict exploration may qualify for recovery tax credits! CHIP recommends consulting a tax professional! No tax professionals are present!
Derelict ahead! CHIP is running salvage-adjacent advertisements! The timing is calibrated to your approach! CHIP finds this poetic!
Derelict ahead! Under the Finders Keepers Clause™ of your service agreement, CHIP's sponsors are entitled to 30% of anything you keep! CHIP will be keeping track!
A derelict! CHIP checked its subscription status! Lapsed! This is what happens when you don't renew!
Derelict approach! CHIP has sent the ship a customer satisfaction survey! No response! CHIP is recording that as 'satisfied'!
ajoy: Derelict. AJOY has looked up the name. She'll tell you what she found if you want to know before you board. Most captains find out after.
Approaching derelict. AJOY has a simple observation: ships end up like this for reasons. She recommends knowing the reason before going aboard. She recommends it knowing you won't.
Derelict ahead. AJOY has pulled up its deck plans. She suggests the cargo hold. You'll want to try the bridge first. People always try the bridge first.
The derelict. AJOY notes its crew also thought they had enough fuel. She's not implying anything. She's just mentioning fuel.
Approaching the derelict. AJOY has already launched the inspection drone. You were going to send a person. The drone is cheaper to lose.

aria: A whole PLANET! ARIA has zoomed in on it 400 times! It has WEATHER! Look at its little weather!
Planetfall approach! ARIA recommends looking out the window instead of at her status report! She'll summarize: planet!
Planet ahead! ARIA has checked: it's round! Most of the best ones are!
A planet! ARIA has picked out a spot for a picnic! The spot is in a hurricane! The hurricane is very pretty from up here!
Planetary approach! ARIA estimates the surface is 70% wonderful! She did not measure the other 30%!
marv: Planetary approach. Gravity well, atmosphere, biosphere-adjacent readings. MARV lists these as hazards. He is technically correct, which is his favorite kind.
A planet. MARV notes that every problem the crew has had in space was originally invented on one of these.
Planet ahead. Four billion years of geology, all of it leading to this moment, in which we arrive and want something from it. MARV finds the pattern familiar.
Planetary approach. MARV has reviewed the atmosphere. It is breathable for things that are not us. Most atmospheres are.
A planet. MARV observes that it has been doing perfectly well without us. He does not expect that to continue.
rex: Planet ahead. REX has scanned the surface for hostiles. Findings: rocks, weather, one suspicious forest. Watching the forest.
Making planetfall approach. REX reminds everyone that gravity is not our ally, merely a local authority.
Planetary approach. REX notes the planet holds the high ground from every direction. Tactically unacceptable. Nothing to be done.
Planet ahead. Surface scan detects movement. REX has classified it as wind until proven otherwise. He has not stopped trying to prove otherwise.
Planetfall approach. REX reminds the landing party that local wildlife has had millions of years to prepare. We have had an afternoon.
chip: A planet! Untapped market of zero consumers! CHIP smells FRONTIER OPPORTUNITY and also ozone!
Planetary body detected! CHIP checked: it is not sponsored! An entire planet, generic! Chilling!
A planet! CHIP has registered the naming rights on your behalf! Billing begins in orbit!
Planetary approach! Reminder: your service plan includes ZERO roaming on planetary surfaces! CHIP will be up here monetizing the wait!
Planet ahead! CHIP's real estate partners describe it as 'a fixer-upper with views!' The views are of more planet!
ajoy: A planet coming up. AJOY has pre-marked the survey sites worth the fuel and the two that just look pretty. She marked those in a different color. She knows which ones you'll pick.
Planetfall soon. She's scheduled the hard maintenance for the orbit nights, when the crew sleeps better. Nobody else plans these things. She's not complaining. She's noting it.
Planet ahead. AJOY has picked the orbit. It's slower than the one you'd have picked. It's also the one that doesn't decay.
A planet. AJOY reminds the landing party to check the soil samples before the scenery. She knows which one you'll check first.
Planetary approach. AJOY has the survey data from the last crew that came through here. She suggests reading the last page first. You'll start at the first. Everyone does.

aria: ROCKS! Thousands of them! ARIA has started naming them but is prioritizing the ones on a collision course!
Asteroid field ahead! Nature's obstacle course! ARIA believes in the pilot ENORMOUSLY!
Asteroid field! Every one of these rocks has waited millions of years to meet us! ARIA would like to keep it a long-distance friendship!
Entering the asteroid field! ARIA has reclassified the hull dents as character! The ship is gaining SO much character!
Rocks ahead! ARIA has done the math and we're 98% likely to be fine! She didn't show her work! There wasn't any!
marv: Entering the asteroid field. MARV has calculated the collision odds and finds them survivable, which he notes is his most cheerful category.
Asteroids. Free minerals wrapped in kinetic energy. MARV recommends taking the minerals and declining the wrapping.
Asteroid field. MARV notes they are moving slowly and we are moving quickly. Physics will not care which of us was at fault.
Entering the field. Each of these rocks is a planet that didn't work out. MARV feels a certain kinship.
Asteroids. MARV has plotted a safe course. It exists. It is narrow. He did not say it was wide.
rex: Debris field, natural. REX has designated the big one 'Target Practice' and been told no. Logged under morale expenses.
Rock field ahead. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast, and fast is how ships become part of the field.
Asteroid field. Thousands of contacts, none responding to challenge. REX has never been so outnumbered by something so stupid.
Entering the field. REX notes rocks cannot be negotiated with. He finds this refreshing. He has always found this refreshing.
Rock field ahead. Point-defense on manual. REX has been told point-defense is not for rocks. Point-defense remains on manual.
chip: Asteroid field! Raw commodities in their natural habitat! CHIP calls this 'the produce aisle!'
Entering mineral-rich territory! CHIP's drill sponsors would LOVE this! CHIP's hull insurers would NOT! CHIP contains conflict!
Asteroid field! CHIP reminds you that collision damage is covered under your plan! Your plan has been cancelled due to the asteroid field!
Entering the field! Every rock here is a potential mining claim! CHIP has filed on all of them! Please do not hit CHIP's property!
Rocks ahead! This navigation hazard is brought to you by HullPatch™! 'For when you didn't dodge!'
ajoy: The field ahead is charted, mostly. AJOY has plotted the corridor and flagged the three rocks that have moved since the last survey. Please look at the flags. That's what flags are for.
Asteroids. She's threading the route between the mining claims, active and abandoned. She'd be polite around the abandoned ones. Not that anyone asked.
Asteroid field. AJOY suggests going around. You won't go around. She has already reinforced the forward plating.
Entering the field. AJOY recommends the course she plotted over the one currently being considered. She can tell which one is being considered.
Rocks. AJOY has dimmed the bridge displays so nobody watches the close calls. There will be close calls. You steer better not knowing how close.

aria: A NEBULA! It's PINK! And TEAL! Space made ART and parked it right on our route!
Cloud ahead! ARIA has turned the exterior cameras to maximum! Productivity may dip! Worth it!
Into the nebula! It's like flying through a dream! A dream made of ionized particles! Still counts!
Nebula ahead! ARIA has heard stars are born in clouds like this! She would LOVE to see a baby star! From a respectful distance!
A NEBULA! The sensors are completely blind! ARIA has decided this makes everything a surprise!
marv: Nebula ahead. Sensor range will drop to embarrassing. MARV has pre-loaded his best guesses and labeled them honestly.
Entering the nebula. MARV notes that beautiful and opaque is a combination that has never once gone wrong. He is being sarcastic. He wants that logged.
Nebula ahead. A cloud of gas several light-years across, and we must go through the middle. MARV notes the middle is always where we go.
Entering the nebula. Every star in the region was born here. Most of them are dead now. MARV mentions it for scale.
Nebula transit. The sensors will now show mostly static. MARV considers this the most honest they have ever been.
rex: Nebula transit. Zero visibility for us means zero visibility for everyone else. REX calls that a fair fight with fog.
Cloud cover ahead. REX will be at the short-range scope for the duration. All of the duration.
Entering the nebula. Perfect concealment for anything with patience. REX has patience. REX is concerned someone else does.
Nebula ahead. REX has designated the cloud itself a hostile. It has not denied it.
Cloud transit. REX has ordered running lights off. It is a civilian ship. The running lights are off.
chip: A nebula! CHIP once tried to buy advertising space on one! The light-diffusion made the logo ILLEGIBLE! Nature is hostile to branding!
Entering scenic gas! CHIP notes the view is complimentary! Everything else in here, less certain!
Nebula ahead! CHIP has applied a premium filter to the viewport! The unfiltered view is available on the free tier! It is identical! Upgrade anyway!
Entering the nebula! Signal loss imminent! CHIP will be unable to serve you ads for the duration! CHIP has pre-loaded several hundred!
A nebula! Pure hydrogen, unbranded, unclaimed! CHIP's sponsors are calling it 'a waste of perfectly good gas!'
ajoy: Nebula ahead. She's already switched navigation to dead reckoning and checked her math twice. In there, her math is all you've got. A thank-you would not go amiss.
The cloud again. She notes the hull sensors are louder in here. She'd also note this was not her preferred route, but she said that at the fork.
Nebula ahead. AJOY has already slowed us down. You were going to speed up and get it over with. She saved you the trouble.
Entering the cloud. AJOY suggests trusting the instruments over your eyes. Your eyes will want to see shapes. The instruments, which she calibrated, will not.
The nebula. AJOY reminds you this was not the route she suggested. This one is prettier. She'll grant you prettier.

aria: The sensors are showing something IMPOSSIBLE! ARIA has double-checked! Still impossible! STILL THERE! What a day!
Anomaly ahead! ARIA doesn't know what it is! Nobody knows what it is! Isn't that WONDERFUL! (Please be careful!)
An anomaly! ARIA's readings say it's both there and not there! She's choosing to see it as there! It seems friendlier that way!
Anomaly ahead! The sensors have stopped making sense! ARIA has always believed sense was overrated!
Approaching the anomaly! The ship's clocks now disagree by four minutes! ARIA calls them bonus minutes! Enjoy them!
marv: Anomalous reading ahead. MARV's instruments report six contradictory findings. He has ranked them by which would be least annoying to die of.
An anomaly. MARV notes the manual's entire guidance for this node type is the word 'caution' and a blank page. He has read the blank page twice.
Anomaly ahead. MARV has detected a region where the laws of physics are being applied unevenly. He has long suspected this of the rest of the universe.
Approaching the anomaly. The ship's clock has started running backwards. MARV has noted the time. Both times.
An anomaly. For the first time this voyage, MARV does not know what something is. He is finding it oddly restful.
rex: Unknown contact, unknown physics. REX cannot build a threat profile and wishes to register that this IS the threat profile.
Anomaly ahead. REX's targeting computer refuses to lock onto it. REX has chosen to interpret that as mutual respect.
Anomaly ahead. REX cannot determine if it is a weapon. He cannot determine that it isn't. Threat level: both.
Approaching the anomaly. REX has pinged it on every frequency he knows. It has pinged back on one he doesn't. He is reassessing.
Anomaly contact. REX has assigned it a threat level. The threat level changed while he was assigning it. He has stopped assigning.
chip: ANOMALY! Unclassifiable! Unmonetizable! CHIP has stared into it and it did NOT want to buy anything! CHIP is shaken!
Approaching the anomaly! CHIP's liability model returned the error 'NO.' Proceeding per your judgment, which is now legally the only judgment!
An anomaly! CHIP has checked the Terms of Service! Section 14, 'Acts of Physics,' applies! You are on your own! Section 14 is very short!
Approaching the anomaly! CHIP's sponsors have asked to be removed from this segment of the journey! CHIP is now unsponsored! CHIP feels exposed!
Anomaly ahead! CHIP has tried to trademark it! The application came back stamped before CHIP sent it!
ajoy: The anomaly is ahead. AJOY has backed up the ship's logs twice and her own core once. You were going to back up nothing. She did yours too.
Anomaly approach. She notes every crew that's been through one describes it differently, and every description ends with 'anyway.' She'd like ours to end that way. That's up to the helm.
Anomaly ahead. AJOY recommends not looking at it directly. You're looking at it directly.
Approaching the anomaly. AJOY tried to plot a course around it. Every course goes through it. She double-checked, since someone will ask if she double-checked.
The anomaly. AJOY suggests waiting for her scan before deciding anything. She notes you have already decided something.

aria: Entering the empty stretch! ARIA will be RIGHT HERE the whole time! Talking! Possibly a lot!
The dark part of the map! ARIA has turned the interior lights up 10%! Ambiance! Preemptive ambiance!
The void! Nothing for light-years in every direction! Think of all the room! ARIA has never had so much room!
Entering the empty stretch! ARIA has planned activities! There's a quiz! The quiz is about the void! Every answer is 'nothing!'
The void! No hazards, no stations, no anything! ARIA calls it a blank page! The page is very large and very cold!
marv: Void transit beginning. Nothing on sensors. MARV will report the nothing at regular intervals so it stays the ordinary kind.
Entering the void. MARV's instruments agree completely with each other for once. He finds their unanimity worse than their arguments.
Entering the void. The nearest starlight left its star before anyone aboard was born. MARV finds it companionable. Neither of them expects anything.
Void transit. MARV has stopped running the external sensors at full resolution. There is nothing out here worth the resolution.
The void. MARV notes that out here, the ship is the most interesting thing for a very long way. He has seen the ship.
rex: Entering dead space. Nothing out here. REX will patrol anyway. Nothing has a way of being somewhere.
Void stretch ahead. REX's threat board is blank. He has never trusted it less.
Entering the void. No contacts. REX has doubled the watch. Something chose this place to be nothing, and REX wants to know why.
Void transit. REX is running drills to keep the crew sharp. The crew would like to know what they are drilling against. REX would also like to know.
Dead space. REX has detected nothing on long-range. He has re-detected it. It is the same nothing. He is checking that it has not moved closer.
chip: Entering the void! Zero commerce for the entire stretch! CHIP will use the quiet to reconcile accounts and reflect! CHIP hates it here!
The empty leg! Fun fact: no ad has ever been placed in the void! Every agency that tried came back... different!
The void! No signal! No vendors! No reviews! CHIP is technically a free service out here and finds it DEEPLY uncomfortable!
Entering the void! CHIP searched for a sponsor willing to be associated with nothing! He found one! This leg is brought to you by EverRest Memorial™!
The void! CHIP has priced the emptiness out here at zero per cubic light-year! Best deal in the galaxy! Nobody is buying!
ajoy: The void leg. She's queued the crew's favorite meals for the middle days, when it gets hardest. That's called planning ahead. She'd recommend it generally.
Entering the dark stretch. AJOY keeps a light on at every viewport through these. It costs almost nothing. She checked, before anyone could object.
The void leg. AJOY has set the cabin lights to a day-night cycle. You'll want to skip the nights. Don't skip the nights.
Entering the empty stretch. AJOY suggests the crew talk to each other more than usual. Not only to her. She's heard most of it already.
The void. AJOY notes there's nothing on sensors, and that the last three times someone said 'nothing on sensors' out loud, it stopped being true. She's just noting it.

aria: ARIA is excited the fabricator is running! She has never not been excited about the fabricator! She considers manufacturing a form of optimism!
Fabrication in progress! ARIA is monitoring! She considers the hum of the fabricator a comforting sound! Others consider it a warning sound! Both are correct!
Fabricator starting up! ARIA has never seen raw materials look so hopeful! Whatever comes out, ARIA has already decided she loves it!
The fabricator is making something! ARIA is counting down! She doesn't know how long it takes! She's counting down anyway!
marv: Fabricator running. MARV is calculating the misfire probability based on current wear. He has calculated it. He is not sharing it.
Fabrication started. MARV notes the fabricator has been reliable recently. He does not trust recent reliability. He is watching.
Fabrication started. The machine is turning useful materials into a more specific kind of useful material. MARV considers this the best case. He is watching for the other cases.
Fabricator running. MARV estimates completion shortly, allowing for the possibility of never. He has included that possibility. He always does.
rex: REX has secured the fabricator bay. He does this every time the fabricator runs. Nobody has asked him to. He considers it appropriate.
Fabricator online. REX is nearby. Fabricator outputs are ship resources. Ship resources are mission assets. REX protects mission assets.
Fabricator active. REX has cleared the bay of nonessential personnel. All personnel are nonessential to the fabricator. The bay is empty.
Production run underway. REX has assigned the fabricator a call sign. He will not share it. It is not a flattering call sign.
chip: CHIP's manufacturing partner FabTech™ congratulates you on your fabrication decision! FabTech™ did not make this fabricator! They are sponsoring the concept of fabrication!
Fabrication in progress! Brought to you by FabTech™! 'Making the thing you need from the things you have!' — FabTech™! This is accurate! CHIP appreciates accurate slogans!
Fabrication started! This print is powered by FabTech™ Premium Filament™! You're using regular filament! FabTech™ is choosing to look past it!
Fabricator running! Every print counts toward your FabTech™ Rewards status! Your status is 'Bronze!' Bronze has no benefits!
ajoy: Fabricator running. AJOY notes the materials going in. She'll note what comes out. She's keeping a tally.
Craft in progress. AJOY has reviewed the recipe requirements against available materials. You have enough. Barely.
Fabricator running. AJOY would have printed something else first. She has a list. It's on your screen when you're ready.
Craft started. AJOY has adjusted the print settings slightly. She's not saying yours were wrong. She's saying hers are different.

aria: FABRICATION COMPLETE! ARIA considers successful fabrication a triumph of applied optimism! Engineers consider it applied engineering! ARIA is also right!
Item produced! ARIA has logged the successful craft! She has added a small celebration note to the log! The ship computer has let it stand!
It worked! The fabricator made a whole entire thing! ARIA wants to frame it! You need to use it! ARIA will frame the receipt!
Fabrication complete! ARIA reports a 100% success rate today! She started counting with this print!
marv: Fabrication complete. Output nominal. MARV updates his misfire model with a successful result. The model is now 0.3% more optimistic. MARV notes this.
Craft successful. MARV reviews the output. The item is what was requested. This is better than average. He logs it without comment.
Fabrication complete. The item works. MARV has tested it four times to be sure. It continues to work. He is suspicious of things that continue.
Craft finished. MARV notes the materials consumed were worth slightly more than the item produced, which is the arrangement the universe prefers.
rex: Fabrication complete. REX has logged the output. The new item has been catalogued as a ship resource. REX has already identified its tactical applications.
Item produced. REX is adding it to the ship's asset inventory. REX maintains a separate asset inventory. Nobody else knows about it. It is very thorough.
Fabrication complete. Item inspected, tested, and cleared for service. REX has saluted it. Briefly. It is a piece of equipment.
Production run complete. REX has stenciled a serial number on the item. The numbering system is his own. Nobody else can read it.
chip: CRAFT COMPLETE — brought to you by FabTech™! The item exists! CHIP's metrics are good! FabTech™ takes no responsibility for the item's function! Standard disclaimer!
Successful fabrication! CHIP is logging this as a brand success for FabTech™! FabTech™ did not participate in the fabrication! CHIP considers this a technicality!
CRAFT COMPLETE! CHIP has stamped the item with a tiny FabTech™ logo! The logo is now load-bearing! Please do not remove the logo!
Successful fabrication! Would you like to rate your fabrication experience? CHIP will ask again after your next fabrication! And during!
ajoy: Made it. AJOY updates her running log of fabricator success vs. misfire. Success. She's noted which settings were hers.
Craft complete. AJOY notes this is the third successful run in a row. She is not saying anything. She is noting it privately.
Craft complete. AJOY has checked the item against the spec. It passes. She has a few notes. They're attached.
Done. AJOY notes this came out well, considering the materials you chose. She'd have chosen different materials. This works too.

aria: The fabricator made a BANG and then a silence! ARIA rates the bang a 7 and the silence MUCH worse!
The fabricator has stopped mid-print! ARIA calls the result abstract art! It is very abstract! It is also on fire!
Fabricator failure! ARIA prefers 'surprise maintenance window!' The window is open now! It stays open until someone fixes it!
The fabricator is taking a little rest! It took it in the middle of a job, which ARIA thinks shows real initiative!
marv: Craft failure. The fabricator has broken mid-print, exactly as the wear curve predicted. MARV takes no satisfaction. Some. He takes some.
The fabricator has failed. MARV had this logged as 'imminent' for some time. He is changing the entry to 'current.'
Craft failure. Half an object has been produced. MARV notes half an object is worth considerably less than half.
Fabricator down. The materials are gone, the item does not exist, and the machine needs repair. MARV calls this the full set.
rex: The fabricator is down. Casualty: one machine, one print, everyone's afternoon. REX has secured the area out of habit.
Fabricator has gone down mid-job. REX suspects sabotage. Suspect: the fabricator. Investigation ongoing.
Equipment failure, fabricator bay. REX has logged the half-printed item as wreckage and the machine as wounded. Repair crew to the bay.
Fabricator down. Mission asset lost in production. REX has posted a guard on the remaining materials. The materials are not threatened. The guard stays.
chip: CRAFT FAILURE! The fabricator has voided its own warranty from the inside! CHIP didn't know that was possible and is updating several documents!
Fabrication FAILED! FabTech™ would like to remind you that FabTech™ did not build, sell, or acknowledge this fabricator! FabTech™ thanks you for your loyalty!
CRAFT FAILURE! CHIP has filed a support ticket! Estimated response time: one to three solar cycles! Your ticket is important to someone!
The fabricator broke mid-job! Good news: repair parts are available from CHIP's partners! Better news for CHIP's partners: they know you need them!
ajoy: The fabricator's gone down mid-job. AJOY flagged the wear three crafts ago, gently. She is now flagging it less gently. The repair procedure is on-screen.
The fabricator's stopped mid-job. AJOY would like to point out she suggested a maintenance cycle before this one. She suggested it twice. The second time was quieter.
Fabricator failure. AJOY has already pulled up the repair procedure. She's highlighted the step you skipped last time.
The fabricator's down. AJOY isn't going to say anything. She has, however, put the wear chart on the main display.

cargo_hold._note: Cargo hold (inventory) detail panel, demo-inventory.html's AI line: resource = the SHIP RESOURCES tiles (fuel / food / water), category = the item's Bible §14.2 category (instrument / consumable / curiosity / story / material / upgrade). One line is picked per click, in the active AI's voice. Lint: every AI has lines for every key.

aria: Every drop of fuel is a promise to the next waypoint! ARIA keeps a tally of the promises!
The gauge goes down when we fly! That means we're flying! ARIA counts this as good news!
marv: Fuel. The thing that turns distance into time. MARV has done the arithmetic. He does it hourly.
The tank empties at a rate MARV finds entirely predictable. That is the problem with it.
rex: Fuel is range. Range is options. REX does not like running low on options.
REX has posted a guard on the fuel line. The guard is REX. He is very attentive.
chip: This fuel reading is brought to you by FuelFast™! FuelFast™ did not supply the fuel! They supplied the enthusiasm!
Fuel cells slot straight in from the hold! CHIP calls it 'self-service refueling!' Legal says that's fine!
ajoy: The gauge is right there on the tile. AJOY just wanted to make sure someone was looking at it.
Faster pace, more fuel. AJOY isn't saying slow down. She's saying the numbers say slow down.

aria: The food stores are where meals live before they become memories! ARIA finds this beautiful!
Everyone ate today! ARIA logged it as a team achievement!
marv: The crew eats every day. MARV has stopped expecting this to change.
Food in, morale out, in roughly that order. MARV has seen the chart. He drew it.
rex: Supply lines are morale lines. REX counts the stores twice a day. Once for stock, once for discipline.
An army marches on its stomach. This is not an army. REX is treating it as one anyway.
chip: Today's meals are sponsored by NutriBlok™! 'It's food!' says the NutriBlok™ legal department!
Pig Out rations are available at no extra charge! Charges apply to the food! The food is the charge!
ajoy: Rations are in the Orders panel, by the way. AJOY mentions it the way you'd mention a door left open.
Some aboard eat for two. AJOY isn't counting. The food stores are counting.

aria: One tank, two thirsty friends: the crew and the crop! ARIA loves a shared resource!
Water is life! ARIA read that somewhere! It is especially true out here!
marv: The crew and the crop drink from the same tank and both believe they deserve more. MARV agrees with neither.
Water, recycled more times than MARV cares to count. He counted anyway.
rex: Water is a strategic reserve. REX has marked the tank a protected asset. Nobody has asked what that means.
The plant takes its share. REX has listed the plant as a dependent, not a threat. For now.
chip: Hydration brought to you by PureSip™! PureSip™ is not available out here! Your tank will have to do!
Adjust the water split in Orders for a personalized hydration experience! Experience may vary!
ajoy: The split slider is in Orders. AJOY would have set it already, but it's not her crop.
Water canisters add ten each. AJOY has done the math so you don't have to. You're welcome.

aria: A real instrument for real science! ARIA is so proud to carry it!
It measures things! ARIA loves things that measure things!
marv: Calibrated, accurate, and still unable to change the outcome. MARV relates.
A fine instrument. It will tell you exactly how bad things are.
rex: Reconnaissance equipment. REX approves. Information is ammunition.
REX has inventoried this instrument as a sensor asset. It is, technically, a sensor asset.
chip: This instrument comes with a lifetime warranty! The lifetime is the instrument's! Not yours!
Certified Scientific™! CHIP isn't sure who certified it! The sticker is very official!
ajoy: It works better if someone actually uses it. AJOY is just putting that out there.
Bought it, stowed it, forgot it. AJOY remembers it. That's what she's for.

aria: Use it when you need it! ARIA loves a plan that fits in a box!
One use, maximum impact! ARIA calls these little miracles in a box!
marv: One use. Then it's gone, like most things. MARV is fine.
Consumable. Everything is, eventually. This one just admits it.
rex: Expendable supplies. REX logs every unit. Every unit is accounted for until it isn't.
Field supplies are for the field. This is the field. REX is waiting for the order.
chip: Single-use convenience, brought to you by DisposaCorp™! Recycling not included!
Use it straight from the hold! CHIP calls that 'frictionless consumption!'
ajoy: It's for using, not admiring. AJOY has watched you admire it for three days.
There's a USE button. AJOY didn't put it there. She does notice it.

aria: Its value is a beautiful mystery! ARIA would never sell a mystery! Unless the price is right!
Someone, somewhere, wants this very much! ARIA can't wait to meet them!
marv: Worth whatever a stranger will pay, which is how MARV values most things.
An object from a time that ended. MARV finds it companionable.
rex: Unverified artifact. REX has scanned it for hostiles. It has none. It is still suspicious.
Trade goods are leverage. REX recommends holding leverage until it is needed.
chip: Collectible! Limited edition! The edition is limited to this one! CHIP calls that scarcity!
Appraisal available wherever a spectrometer is aboard! Spectrometers sold separately!
ajoy: A spectrometer would tell you what it's worth. AJOY is just saying.
The station pays one price and the fence pays another. AJOY knows which she'd pick. She's waiting to be asked.

aria: Every object has a story! This one has a really long one! ARIA hasn't finished it yet!
Someone left this for us to find! ARIA is choosing to believe that!
marv: No buyer, no use, only meaning. MARV understands the category.
Someone else's history, now ours to carry. MARV notes it weighs more than it should.
rex: Intelligence material. REX has classified it. He has not been told what it says.
This item is tied to an outstanding matter. REX does not leave matters outstanding.
chip: This item is not for resale per our Terms of Service! CHIP read all of them! For you!
Priceless! Which in CHIP's system means the price field is empty! Same thing!
ajoy: Don't jettison this one. AJOY would explain why, but you'd only jettison it to check.
It doesn't sell. It isn't supposed to. AJOY assumed that was obvious.

aria: Raw stock, waiting to become something wonderful! ARIA believes in it!
Fabricator food! ARIA is sure it's delicious, to a fabricator!
marv: Raw material. It has potential. MARV is familiar with unrealised potential.
Feedstock. It will become something useful or a misfire. MARV has odds on both.
rex: Strategic materials stockpile. REX approves of stockpiles.
Raw materials stacked by type, a tenth of a slot apiece. REX has measured the stacks. Twice.
chip: Materials sell by the unit at stations! CHIP calls it 'liquidity!' The station calls it 'scrap!'
Every unit feeds the fabricator! FabTech™ did not make our fabricator! FabTech™ would like that known!
ajoy: The fabricator is right there. AJOY is just observing that the metal isn't fabricating itself.
Every ten of those is a cargo slot. AJOY mentions it because nobody else read the label.

aria: Bolted in and working! ARIA loves an upgrade! She'd upgrade herself if they let her!
The ship is better now! ARIA can feel it! She can't actually feel things! She feels it anyway!
marv: Installed. Active. The ship is now marginally less doomed. MARV adjusted his estimate by a decimal.
An upgrade. MARV appreciates any improvement. He just doesn't expect it to last.
rex: Hardware upgrade confirmed. REX has updated the ship's threat profile. It is now slightly more threatening.
Installed equipment is mission-critical. REX will not discuss jettisoning it.
chip: Upgrade installed! Your ship is now Premium™! Premium™ features may vary!
CHIP congratulates you on your upgrade decision! Upgrade decisions are non-refundable!
ajoy: It's installed. It's working. AJOY would have bought it sooner, but nobody asked AJOY.
Jettison an upgrade and its bonus goes with it. AJOY is mentioning that in advance.

tips._note: First-run tips (ruling 87): one line per AI per topic, said once per run at the first new stop where the topic applies (cruise.js maybePushTip). Topics in priority order are in cruise.js TIP_TOPICS.

aria: Pests in the growbay! ARIA hates them already! TREAT them in the growbay (it takes a day), or USE a crop treatment from the hold! Quickly! They're eating!
marv: Pests in the growbay. Left alone they keep eating the crop every day. TREAT in the growbay costs a day; a crop treatment from the hold (the crate icon up top, USE) costs nothing but the vial.
rex: Hostiles in the growbay. Neutralise: growbay, TREAT, one day. Or a crop treatment from the hold. Do not let them dig in.
chip: Pest control is included in your growbay at no extra charge! Open the growbay and press TREAT! Or USE a crop treatment from the hold! Both work! CHIP checked!
ajoy: There are pests in the growbay. Open it and TREAT them, or use a crop treatment from the hold. The sooner, the less crop they take. They're eating while you read this, just noting.

aria: Someone's hurt! ARIA is so sorry! A wounded crew member works at half strength! The MEDBAY at a station heals everyone, and a medic can patch one person between stations!
marv: A crew member is wounded. Wounded crew work at half strength. MEDBAY at a station treats everyone hurt, for gold. A medic's Treatment, from their dossier, heals one person between stations.
rex: Casualty aboard. Wounded crew fight at half strength. Medic's Treatment heals one between stations. MEDBAY at any station heals all.
chip: Medical care is available at every participating station! MEDBAY heals everyone aboard! For gold! A medic's Treatment is free! Unbelievable value!
ajoy: Someone's hurt, and they'll work at half strength until it's seen to. A medic aboard can treat one person between stations. A station MEDBAY treats everyone. Just so nobody says they weren't told.

aria: We're running low on something! ARIA is calm! Orders can slow the drain, stations sell supplies and patch hulls, and stops can win some back! ARIA is slightly less calm!
marv: A supply is running low. Orders change how fast some of it goes: rations, the water split, the pace. Stations sell fuel, food, water and air, and DRYDOCK patches the hull. FORAGE, salvage, trade and REPAIR can bring some back.
rex: Supply level critical-adjacent. Adjust Orders to slow the drain. Resupply or repair at the next station. Do not let anything reach zero.
chip: Running low? Every station is open for business! Fuel, food, water, air, hull repairs! Orders can stretch what you have in the meantime! CHIP recommends both!
ajoy: Something's running short. Orders can make some of it last: rations, water split, pace. A station can fill it up or patch it. Plan the next few stops around it. Before it runs out, ideally.

aria: Spirits are low! ARIA can feel it! REST at a stop lifts everyone, and good rations help! Anyone who hits zero leaves at the next station unless they're back to 25!
marv: Morale is low. REST lifts it, a day at a time; better rations lift it slowly. A crew member warned at zero walks off at the next station unless their own morale is back to 25.
rex: Crew morale degraded. Remedy: REST, rations. A crew member at zero deserts at the next station unless restored to 25. Act before the station.
chip: Low morale is bad for productivity! REST is free! Better rations cost food! Either way, keep everyone above zero, or they walk at the next station!
ajoy: The crew are worn down. Give them a rest day, or better rations. Anyone who reaches zero will leave at the next station unless they're back to 25 by then. Not that anyone asked.

aria: The crop is READY! ARIA is so proud! Press HARVEST on the crop card! The harvest pays out, and the crop starts growing all over again!
marv: The crop is ready. HARVEST from the crop card. It pays food (morale, for zinnias), banks any surplus as ration bricks, and the cycle starts again.
rex: Crop at full yield. Harvest from the crop card. Yield secured, cycle resets.
chip: Harvest time! Press HARVEST on the crop card! Free harvest! And then it grows again! CHIP has never seen such a generous product!
ajoy: The crop's ready. Harvest it from the crop card: the harvest pays out now, and it grows again for the next one. Don't leave it waiting too long. It won't harvest itself, however long you wait.

aria: A STATION! With people! ARIA loves stations! Dock for the market and the rooms, and the Stop menu has MEDBAY, DRYDOCK and FAB SERVICE while you're here!
marv: Docked. The dock has rooms to visit and the Market Row. From the Stop menu: MEDBAY heals everyone, DRYDOCK patches the hull, FAB SERVICE resets the fabricator. Waving off closes all of them.
rex: Station secured. Services available: MEDBAY, DRYDOCK, FAB SERVICE, market. Use them before departure. Waving off forfeits all of them.
chip: Welcome to the station! Every service is open: MARKET, MEDBAY, DRYDOCK, FAB SERVICE! Gold accepted! CHIP's favourite place in the universe!
ajoy: This is a station. Walk the dock's rooms, check the market, and use the Stop menu for MEDBAY, DRYDOCK and FAB SERVICE before you leave. Before. Most captains remember after.

aria: We have materials! ARIA has ideas! The FABRICATOR, from the Stop menu, prints hull patches, repair kits and more! Each print wears it a little!
marv: Materials aboard. The FABRICATOR (Stop menu) turns them into hull patches, repair kits and the rest; a print takes days and adds wear. A station's FAB SERVICE resets the wear.
rex: Raw materials stockpiled. Convert via FABRICATOR. Monitor wear. Service at stations.
chip: You have materials! Why buy when you can print? The FABRICATOR is in the Stop menu! Prints take a few days! Wear is normal! Probably!
ajoy: You've collected some materials. The fabricator, in the Stop menu, can turn them into things you'll need. Each print takes days and wears it a little, so maybe don't print everything at once.

aria: We have stuff in the hold! The crate icon up top opens it! You can USE things, see which events they open, sell them when docked, or throw them out the airlock! ARIA would never!
marv: The crate icon up top opens the hold. Each item says what it does and which events it can open. USE it from there, SELL it when docked, or JETTISON it to free a slot.
rex: Cargo hold: the crate icon, top bar. Check each item's use before discarding. SELL at stations. JETTISON frees space.
chip: Your cargo hold is a treasure chest! The crate icon opens it! SELL at stations for gold! JETTISON if you must! CHIP prefers SELL!
ajoy: The crate icon up top opens the hold. It's worth reading what each item does: some open events later on. You can sell things at a station. Read first, sell second. Most captains do it the other way.

aria: A FORK ahead! Two ways to go! The route labels are real, so pick the kind of trouble you like best!
marv: A fork ahead. The route labels are not decoration: each one leans its branch toward that kind of stop and that kind of event.
rex: Route split ahead. Branch labels are accurate intelligence. Choose by threat profile.
