chip: A fork! Two routes! Two experiences! The labels tell you what you're buying! CHIP respects honest labelling!
ajoy: There's a fork coming. The labels on each route tell you honestly what it leans toward. Choose the one your ship can afford, not the one that sounds fun.

aria: Welcome aboard! At any stop, STOP opens the Stop menu! Mine, scan, rest, repair, trade! Each one takes time and effort! RESUME flies us on!
marv: At each stop, STOP opens the Stop menu: the things you can do here. Each verb costs time and the crew's effort, which costs morale. RESUME flies on to the next stop.
rex: Standard procedure: STOP opens operations at each stop. Each action costs time and effort. RESUME continues the mission.
chip: At every stop, press STOP for the full menu of services! Every action has a time cost and an effort cost! RESUME when you're done! Enjoy!
ajoy: At each stop, press STOP to see what you can do here. Every action takes time and some of the crew's effort. Press RESUME when you're ready to fly on. After looking, ideally.

aria: Tip! The readout strip under the gauges opens ORDERS! Pace, rations and the water split! ARIA likes LUDICROUS! ARIA has been told not to choose!
marv: The readout strip opens Orders: pace trades speed for fuel and morale, rations trade food for morale, and the water split shares water between the crew and the crop.
rex: Orders: click the readout strip. Pace, rations, water allocation. Set them for the stretch ahead.
chip: Customise your voyage! Click the readout strip for ORDERS! Pace! Rations! Water split! All included!
ajoy: Click the readout strip to open Orders. Pace, rations and the water split decide how fast you travel and how fast you use things up. The defaults are not a strategy, just noting.

aria: The crop card opens the GROWBAY! Water, tending, threats, and TREAT for pests! ARIA visits every day!
marv: The crop card opens the growbay: its health, its water, its threats, who tends it, TREAT for pests, and the harvest.
rex: Primary objective: the crop. Crop card opens the growbay. Monitor health and threats.
chip: The crop card is your window into the growbay! Health! Water! Pests! Harvest! Everything a growing business needs!
ajoy: Click the crop card to open the growbay. It shows what's helping and hurting the crop, and that's where you treat pests and harvest. Worth a look before something goes wrong. Not after.

aria: MAP shows the whole trail! Where we are, where we're going, all the forks! The ??? stops are surprises! SCAN tells you what's coming!
marv: MAP shows the trail: where you are, what's ahead, the forks. A ??? stop is unscanned; SCAN at a stop reads what the next one holds.
rex: MAP: full route overview. Unknown stops marked ???. SCAN for advance intelligence.
chip: The MAP is free to use! It shows every stop and every fork! ??? means a mystery! SCAN removes the mystery! For a day!
ajoy: MAP shows the whole trail and the forks ahead. The ??? stops are unknown until you SCAN for them. Guessing is also an option. Just not a good one.

greet: You look like someone with cargo space.
Come in, come in. Everything's for sale except the chair. The chair has history.
Ah. A customer. I'd almost forgotten the feeling.
Welcome. Browse freely. The prices are firm and the shelves are not.
You have the walk of someone who needs something. Everyone does, this far out.
Stars guide you — to my inventory, specifically.
A ship! With money on it, presumably! Come in, presumably!
pitch: This one came off a freighter that doesn't officially exist. The discount reflects that.
I have exactly one of these left. I also had exactly one of these last month.
It works. I've seen it work. The man who saw it work with me is unavailable for comment.
Half price, because the box is dented. The box protects an item that cannot dent. Think about it.
This is the last honest price between here and the colony. After me, it's all margins.
I'm not saying it's rare. The manufacturer said it's rare. Blame them.
Priced to move, because I'm priced to move — my dock fees double at midnight.
accept: Done. You won't regret it, and if you do, regret is non-refundable.
A pleasure. The receipt is implied.
Sold. Handle it like it's fragile. It isn't, but handle it that way anyway.
Good choice. That's the one I would have kept, if keeping things paid.
refuse: That's not an offer, that's an opinion. I don't stock opinions.
I'd sooner give it away. I won't do that either.
No. But I respect the attempt. Try again with money.
The item costs what it costs. The universe is unfair everywhere, not just here.
farewell: Safe travels. Tell people about my shop. Kind people.
Off you go. Come back solvent.
Fly safe. Everything out there is trying to make you a customer of someone worse.
Goodbye. If anyone asks, you paid full price. Have some dignity, both of us.

greet: Oh. A ship. Haven't seen a ship in... what year is it? Don't tell me. Let me guess wrong first.
Hello, hello. Don't mind the mess. The mess was here before me and it'll be here after.
Visitors. Well. The kettle's broken, but the sentiment of a kettle is available.
You're real, yes? Quick check. Wave your arms. Good. Wonderful. Come in.
ramble: I came out here in a ship half the size of yours and twice as loud. The noise kept me company until it didn't, and then the quiet did, and the quiet turned out to be better conversation.
Used to run cargo for the colony office. Then the colony office became two colony offices, and both of them fired me, which I consider a kind of promotion.
There was a woman on Enceladus station who could fix anything with a spot welder and contempt. I think about her every time something breaks. Something breaks a lot.
The stars look different out here. Not the arrangement. The attitude. Closer in, they twinkle. Out here they just look at you.
Kept a garden once, in a cargo pod. One tomato plant. Best conversation I ever had was with that plant, and I include this one.
You know what I miss? Doors that other people walk through. That's the whole list.
offer: Take it. I've got no use for it, and things should be used. That's my whole philosophy. Also the kettle's broken.
Here. Before you argue: I found it, I don't need it, and arguing with me is how people end up staying for dinner.
You should have this. Don't ask what it cost me. It cost me nothing, and I want the mystique.
A word of advice, free of charge, which is exactly what advice is worth: the shortcut past the next marker isn't.
farewell: Go on, then. The quiet and I have things to not discuss.
Safe journey. Wave at the void for me. It doesn't wave back, but it notices.
Goodbye. Come back in a few years. I'll be here, or I'll be a very interesting absence.
Off with you. And oil that airlock hinge. I could hear it from here. It kept me up.

hail: Cut your engines. Let's keep this professional.
Well now. A ship, alone, this far out. Somebody's been brave with the route planning.
Attention, little vessel. This is a business call.
Don't run. Everyone runs. It embarrasses us both and burns your fuel.
Heave to. This is the part where you heave to.
Nice ship. Shame about the next ten minutes.
demand: Cargo. Fuel. Whatever's shiny. In that order, and quickly.
You give us a cut, we give you the rest of your journey. Everyone leaves solvent. Mostly you leave.
The toll out here is whatever we say it is. Today it's whatever you have that's heavy.
Open the hold. Consider it a tax. The government is me.
Half your hold buys all of your future. Bargain rates today.
We take a cut, you keep the rest and the breathing. Standard terms.
accept: Smart. You'd be surprised how rare smart is out here.
Pleasure doing business. That's a joke. It was only a pleasure for one of us.
Good. See how easy? Tell the next ship how easy.
Taken. You get to keep the rest, including your day. Cheap at the price.
refuse: Wrong answer. There was a right one. It was shorter.
So that's how it is. Fine. That's how it is.
I gave you the polite version first. Remember that later.
defeated: This is the part where I say you'll regret it. You probably won't. Lucky sod.
Fine. FINE. The sector's gone soft anyway.
You fight like someone with something to protect. That was our mistake, then.

greet: Welcome aboard. Keep your dock fees paid and your complaints brief.
Ah, the new arrival. We logged your approach. Twice. Your transponder stutters.
Captain. Good. I prefer talking to captains. Fewer illusions.
Welcome to the station. The rules are posted. The exceptions are not.
address: Let me be direct, because the alternative takes longer.
I'll say this once, and then I'll say it again, because once never works.
Here's the situation, minus the parts you don't need.
Listen carefully. This station runs on schedules and forbearance, and we're low on both.
approve: Approved. Don't make me remember approving it.
Fine. Logged and stamped. The stamp is the important part.
Granted. You'd be amazed what I say no to, so appreciate this properly.
Yes. Go. Before I think about it harder.
refuse: No. And before you ask: also no.
Denied. The reason is a paragraph long and boring. Trust the summary.
That's not happening. Not on my station, not on my shift, not on appeal.
Request denied. File a complaint if you like. The complaint box is real and the emptying schedule is not.
dismiss: We're done here. The door knows the way.
That's all. Clear the office. Somebody worse is waiting.
Dismissed. Fly safe. It reflects on my station when people don't.
Go on. And take your paperwork. It stopped being my paperwork when you picked it up.

greet: Sit. Breathe. Tell me which of those was difficult.
New patient. Wonderful. Allergies, implants, lies? List them in that order.
Welcome to medbay. The smell is antiseptic. The antiseptic is working. Everything is fine.
Come in. Don't touch the tray. Everyone touches the tray.
assess: Hold still. The scanner is old and takes offense easily.
Mm. Mm-hm. Interesting. Don't worry about which kind of interesting.
Your readings are within range. The range was set by people who never left orbit, but within range.
I've seen worse. Recently. On this table. That's the good news.
treat: This will sting. I say that so you trust me about the things that won't.
Done. The bandage is doing ninety percent of the work. The other ten percent is you leaving it alone.
Take these. With food. Real food, not the bricks. Find real food first. That's the hard part of the prescription.
Fixed. It'll ache when it rains. There's no rain in space. You're welcome.
bill: The treatment was the easy part. Here's the invoice.
Payment's due before departure. Medbay policy. I've heard every objection and rated them.
That'll be the posted rate. The posted rate is behind you. Don't gasp, it unsettles the other patients.
The station bills for supplies. I bill for patience. Only one of those is negotiable.
farewell: Out you go. Come back never, professionally speaking.
You're cleared. Hydrate. Everyone forgets to hydrate.
Goodbye. If the symptoms return, they're someone else's symptoms. Check your crew.
Off the table. Next time, lead with what actually happened.

greet: Yeah? Talk while I hold this. It's load-bearing and so am I.
Customer. Give me a second. This panel and I are at a delicate point in the negotiation.
Welcome to the shop. Mind the coils. The coils do not mind you.
You need something fixed, replaced, or explained. I do two of those cheerfully.
diagnose: Found it. You're not going to like it. I don't like it, and I get paid to like it.
The good news: it's fixable. The other news: everything is fixable. That's not a comfort, that's a warning about scope.
Whoever repaired this last did their best. Their best is why you're here.
It's the coupling. It's always the coupling. One day it won't be, and I'll retire on the strangeness of that day.
quote: Parts, labor, and a surcharge for what the labor discovered. Here's the number.
I can do it fast, cheap, or correctly. Pick one. Yes, one.
The estimate assumes nothing else is wrong. That assumption has never once held.
That price includes me not describing what I found in your intake manifold. Frankly, it's a bargain.
install: Done. It'll hold longer than the part it replaced, which is a low bar I have nonetheless personally raised.
In and running. The hum is normal. The other hum, tell someone immediately.
Fitted. Don't let anyone 'adjust' it. Especially anyone confident.
farewell: Fly gentle. Machines remember.
Go on. And stop redlining the intake. I can tell. I can always tell.
Done and done. Next time bring the ship in before it sounds like that.
Clear skies. The invoice follows you electronically, like a loyal pet.

greet: Careful where you step. Everything in here is alive, including my mood.
A visitor. Are those crop questions I smell, or are you lost? Both is common.
Welcome to the greenhouse. Voices low. They're not sensitive, but I am.
Come in. Touch nothing green. The non-green things, also nothing.
diagnose: Show me the leaves. The leaves never lie. Crews lie. Leaves, never.
Mm. Overwatered. Everyone overwaters. Affection is the leading cause of drowning.
Your soil's tired. Soil gets tired. It's doing all the work while everyone watches the leaves.
This is stress growth. Something in your growbay is frightening this plant. Find it. Plants have very short lists of fears.
sell: These seeds are viable. I germinated their siblings myself. We're practically family.
The nutrient mix costs what it costs because of what's in it. What's in it is the reason your crop lives. Circular, but true.
One packet. Genuine stock, station-certified, and I will absolutely know if you resell it.
This strain survived three owners who didn't deserve it. It'll survive you. That's a sales pitch.
advise: Free advice: talk to it or don't, but pick one. Plants hate inconsistency more than neglect.
Whatever your schedule says, water at the same ship-hour every day. Rhythm is nutrition.
If the leaves point at the door, your airflow's wrong. Plants always point at the problem. Learn their grammar.
Don't harvest early out of fear. Fear-harvesting is how you end up with a cargo hold full of almosts.
farewell: Go. And whatever you do to that crop, do it on purpose.
Goodbye. Send me a leaf sometime. People send letters. Leaves are better.
Safe travels. Remember: the crop doesn't know you're behind schedule. Keep it that way.
Off you go. May your greens outlive your problems.

greet: Mind the wet patch. Been chasing it three days. It moves.
Oh, don't mind me. Nobody does. It's the best part of the job.
Welcome aboard. You want the map by the lift. The map lies about level three, but it means well.
New face. I'd shake hands but you've seen what I mop.
remark: Been maintaining this corridor since before it had a name. It had a number. The number was better.
Stations don't get dirty, you know. People bring the dirt. Stations just hold it for them.
That light's flickered for six years. I've reported it forty times. At this point we're both part of the architecture.
Quietest shift is third watch. Just me, the hum, and whatever lives behind panel nine. We don't bother each other.
warn: I'd steer clear of dock four today. No reason I can put in writing.
Watch yourself around the customs office this week. The new officer alphabetizes. Alphabetizers escalate.
Wouldn't eat at the noodle place till Thursday. Thursday's when the good pot comes back from repair.
Keep your ship locked at night berth. Not saying why. Saying it twice, though: locked.
gossip: Heard the quartermaster's been selling manifest slots. Heard it from the manifest.
The captain's office got new carpet. Third time this year. Nobody spills that much coffee. Nobody.
Fella came through last week asking the same questions you're asking. Left in a hurry. Left a good tip, though, so, balanced.
They say the station's changing owners again. The vending machines always know first. Watch the prices.
Dock officer's been whistling all week. Somebody's getting audited. Whistling means audits. Write that down.
New freight contract came through Tuesday. How do I know? Tuesday's mop water. Different grease entirely.
farewell: Mind how you go. And you didn't hear anything from me, mostly because nobody remembers I talk.
Off you pop. Leave the corridor how you found it. I'll know.
Safe flying. I'd say visit again but people who visit twice start noticing things.
Go on then. I've got a wet patch to out-think.

challenge: Hold it right there. Identification, itinerary, and the short version of your intentions.
Stop. This section's restricted. The sign says so, and I'm what the sign escalates to.
You. Yes, you. Nobody walks that casually who's actually casual.
Papers. And before you say the system's down: the system is me.
warn: First warning. There's no second warning. There's paperwork, and you don't want to be paperwork.
Consider this a courtesy. I'm not known for courtesy, so weigh it accordingly.
Whatever you're about to do, the cameras and I would prefer you didn't.
Step back from the cordon. The cordon is for everyone. Yes, even captains. Especially captains.
detain: Right, that's it. Hands where I can log them.
You're coming with me. It's a short walk and a long form.
Detained. The word sounds worse than the room. The room's fine. The word does the work.
Don't run. The station is a circle. They always run, and it's always a circle.
dismiss: Cleared. Move along. Being interesting once is plenty.
You check out. Go. And stay checked out, it's less work for us both.
Fine. You're free to go. The cameras will miss you.
On your way. And tell your crew the docks close at signal-curfew. They know. Tell them anyway.

quirks: They check a wrist device that means nothing to you.
They have the tired posture of someone who has explained things to committees.
They drink from a mug with a faded logo of a company that no longer exists.
Their antennae twitch toward you before their head turns.
Their wings buzz once, briefly — punctuation, or weather, or both.
Their compound eyes catch the light in a hundred small copies of you.
Their mandibles click in a rhythm that might be speech, or might be digestion.
They stand so still that dust has opinions about settling on them.
Something shifts inside them with a sound like a patient landslide.
When they finally move, it is all at once, like a decision made geologically.
There is lichen on their shoulder. Neither of them seems concerned.
Their transport tank sloshes with each gesture.
Ripples cross their surface when something amuses them — something just did.
Their form leans toward you slightly, the way a tide considers a shore.
Light passes through part of them and comes out a different color.
They blink with the wrong eyelid first.
Their head tilts with slow precision, like a dial being set.
A tongue flick samples the air between you, and finds it informative.
They are unblinking for exactly as long as it takes you to notice.
A small fan somewhere spins up, then stops.
Their LEDs blink in a pattern that is almost, but not quite, polite.
They address you, briefly, by what appears to be your hull registration number.
One of their servos hums a note. It is not a musical note. It is trying.
You elect not to think about it too hard.
The translator renders their pause as '[pause]', which is somehow worse.
They respond to your question slightly before you finish asking it.
Their outline is perfectly clear except in your peripheral vision, where it declines to commit.

aria: A vigorous exchange of ideas approaches!
Combat! How exciting. Please don't die.
ARIA has queued her battle playlist! It is one song! It is very good though!
Visitors! With weapons! ARIA has set the shields to Welcoming!
marv: Combat initiated. Probability of hull damage: high. I have stopped rounding it down. Proceeding.
Combat. Again. MARV has updated the growbay's insurance estimate mid-sentence.
Hostile vessel on approach. MARV filed this encounter under inevitable four sectors ago.
Engagement begins. The plants have not been consulted. They rarely are.
rex: Hostile contact. Engaging.
Threat assessment complete. Engage at will.
Contact confirmed. REX has been ready for this since manufacture.
Bandit closing. Weapons free on your mark.
chip: Combat detected. StellarSeal hull insurance is available at participating stations.
Combat engaged! CHIP reminds all parties that violence voids most warranties, including theirs!
Hostile encounter! This combat is brought to you by StellarSeal, the sealant that seals!
Combat mode activated! By engaging, you agree to the Terms of Engagement, sections 1 through 900!
ajoy: You could have taken the other path. She did mention the other path.
AJOY has logged the moment the fight became unavoidable. It was eleven minutes ago. She said nothing. She is saying it now.
They are hailing with their guns. She did suggest the quieter route.
A fight, then. She has moved the good seedlings to the inner bay. Someone had to.

aria: A wonderful application of focused light!
Light! Going VERY fast! At them!
Shot away! ARIA rates it ten out of ten!
Direct delivery of energy! They'll feel SO energized!
marv: Firing. The growbay is aware.
Discharge complete. The universe is now marginally warmer and they are marginally fewer.
Weapon discharged. Somewhere, a probability collapses unhappily.
Firing. MARV computed the trajectory. It was the easy part.
rex: Firing. Center mass.
Rounds out. Watch the spread.
Shot out. Keep it on them.
Weapons release. Adjust and repeat.
chip: Discharge logged for warranty purposes.
Shot fired! Ammunition is non-refundable once discharged!
Firing! Every shot earns StarPoints, redeemable at no locations currently!
Discharge complete! Please rate your shooting experience after the engagement!
ajoy: You fired. She'd have aimed for the engines, but the rest of the ship is also a target.
That one was aimed well. She mentions it because she recalibrated the mount last week. No reason.
You fired. She would have waited a second longer. It hit anyway.
A good shot. She would not have chosen that moment, but it is your ship. Apparently.

aria: A graceful pirouette in the void!
WHEEE! Tactically!
We're dancing! The enemy is not invited!
ARIA calls this move The Brave Leaf!
marv: Evading. Statistical improvement: marginal.
Evasion pattern executed. Dignity: reduced. Hull: preserved. Acceptable trade.
Course altered. The enemy will now aim at where we were. Briefly.
Evading. The ship lurches. So does MARV's outlook, though there was not far to go.
rex: Evasive pattern. Standard.
Displace and reset. Textbook.
Jinking. Keep them guessing.
Break turn. Hold the new heading.
chip: Evasive maneuvers cost an estimated 0.4 cents in fuel.
Evasive maneuver logged! Your insurance premium appreciates your caution even if nobody else does!
Evasion engaged! Sudden lurching is a free feature of your Economy Hull plan!
Dodging! CHIP reminds passengers that seatbelts are a premium add-on!
ajoy: You moved. She had already nudged the heading. Coincidence, surely.
A clean sidestep. She'll credit the pilot. The thruster trim was hers, but she'll credit the pilot.
You turned left. She would have turned right. Both work, apparently.
Evasion complete. She asks only that you warn the growbay next time.

aria: Their shot went WHOOSHING past! How neat!
They missed us entirely! They must be shy!
Not a scratch! ARIA believes the ship is simply too nice to hit!
Total miss! The void is on our side today!
marv: Direct hit avoided. The math is uncharitable about repeats.
Missed entirely. MARV will not be revising his outlook on the basis of one data point.
Clean miss. Their shot continues into deep space, where it will hit something in nine thousand years.
Full evasion. The pilot is briefly better than the odds. It will not last.
rex: Clean dodge. Acknowledged.
Zero contact. Good flying.
Round passed wide. Pilot did their job.
Missed us clean. Stay sharp.
chip: Full evasion logged. Your no-claims discount is preserved.
Zero damage detected! Your hull's resale value thanks you!
Complete miss! This dodge was sponsored by AgileThrust Maneuvering Jets!
Clean dodge! No claim, no paperwork, no joy for the adjusters!
ajoy: The shot missed. She'd moved the shielding to that side. Nobody asked, so she's telling you.
A complete miss. She had already reinforced that panel, so it would have been fine. But fine.
They missed. She would like the record to show she said the pilot was worth bringing.
Nothing hit. You are welcome to thank the pilot. She already has.

aria: The engineer is doing wonderful welding things!
Good as new! Well, good as slightly used!
The hole is gone! ARIA always knew it was temporary!
Patched! The hull is now forty percent tape and one hundred percent spirit!
marv: Hull patch applied. Structural integrity: temporarily plausible.
Breach sealed. The patch is rated for roughly the next breach.
Hull repaired. MARV has added the patch to the list of things that will fail later.
Patch complete. The ship is now slightly less likely to become several ships.
rex: Patch holds. Continue.
Breach sealed. Back in the fight.
Damage control complete. Return to station.
Hull plated. Good work, engineer.
chip: Hull patch covered under your premium maintenance plan.
Hull patched! Genuine HullMend parts used where available! Elsewhere, gum!
Repair complete! This patch is covered by a ninety-second limited warranty!
Hull restored! Remember: unauthorized repairs may void your void coverage!
ajoy: You repaired the ship. She flagged that panel before the fight, but during also works.
Patched. She had flagged that seam three jumps ago. Now it is fixed. Lovely.
The engineer sealed the breach. She held the light. Nobody asked her to hold the light.
Hull repaired. It is nice to fix things before they get worse. Or after. After also works.

aria: The drive is humming! It does that!
The drive is winding up! ARIA is helping by believing in it VERY hard!
Charging up! The stars are going to be SO stretchy!
The drive is warming! ARIA has told it the destination is lovely!
marv: FTL charging. Enemy fire incoming for the duration.
FTL spooling. The next several moments will be statistics. MARV will narrate none of them.
Drive charging. MARV estimates enough time remains for several regrets.
Spooling. The enemy has also noticed. They tend to.
rex: FTL spinup engaged. Hold position.
Drive charging. Weapons stay hot until the stars smear.
Drive spinning up. Keep them busy.
Charge building. Nobody touches the throttle.
chip: FTL prep is a great time to think about extended warranties.
FTL prep initiated! Please ensure all loose items and regrets are stowed!
FTL charging! While you wait, why not browse our catalogue of discount escape pods?
Jump drive warming! Estimated wait time: longer than you would like!
ajoy: You are leaving. She suggested leaving earlier, but leaving is leaving.
Spooling. She has run this maneuver more often than you have. Please let her concentrate.
Charging. She would have started this two turns ago, but here we are.
The drive is spooling. Please do not touch anything. She means you.

aria: AND we're GONE! See you, pirate!
Jumped! Fresh space! It smells brand new!
Escape successful! Running away is just advancing somewhere else!
Gone! ARIA hopes the pirate finds a nice hobby!
marv: FTL achieved. Threat vector: relocated.
Jump complete. The problem is now behind us, where problems wait.
Arrived elsewhere. Fuel spent. The pirate keeps the moral victory.
FTL complete. We are now somewhere we have not yet been shot at.
rex: Jump complete. Disengaged.
Clear of contact. Stand down.
Out of range. Weapons cold.
Exfil complete. Log the bandit.
chip: Successful jump. StellarFTL Premium thanks you.
Jump complete! Fuel charges will appear on your next statement!
You have arrived! Please rate your getaway from one to five stars!
Escape confirmed! StellarFTL reminds you: running is free, fuel is not!
ajoy: You escaped. She'd log it as a retreat, but escape reads better. She'll allow it.
We left. She had the coordinates ready earlier, if anyone had asked.
Jump complete. The pirate is somebody else's problem now. The route was ours. She did flag the route.
Gone. She notes the jump was smooth. Whoever was at the helm will say it was them.

aria: They're shooting! That seems hostile!
Incoming! Everyone think sturdy thoughts!
They're sending us their lasers! How generous!
We've been hit! Character is being built right now!
marv: Hostile fire. Hull integrity reducing as expected.
They are firing again. Persistence: noted. Aim: improving. MARV dislikes both.
Incoming. MARV has already reallocated the dent.
They fire. The hull absorbs it, as it absorbs most things, without complaint.
rex: Incoming. Brace.
Taking fire. Hold the line.
Rounds incoming. Absorb and return.
Hit taken. Still operational.
chip: Damage sustained. Subject to deductible.
Hostile discharge detected! Remember: dents are character, holes are claims!
Impact detected! Your deductible has been met! Congratulations!
Incoming fire! CHIP reminds you this ship's paint is a limited edition!
ajoy: Incoming. She saw this coming three turns ago and said so. Quietly, apparently.
Incoming fire. She has angled the good side of the hull toward it. The ship has a good side. It does now.
They fired. She saw it coming. She sees most things coming.
Hit taken. She had mentioned the shields, once, quietly, in a previous sector.

aria: They look quite injured! Maybe they'll be friends!
Their ship is doing the sad smoke thing! Almost done!
They're almost out of ship! Go team!
They're venting so much! Maybe they're just excited!
marv: Enemy hull critical. Surrender probability: rising.
Enemy structural integrity approaching negotiation territory. Or debris territory. Adjacent territories.
Enemy hull failing. Their outlook now matches MARV's.
Target critical. One more volley, or one more apology.
rex: Target weakened. Press the advantage.
They're breaking. Finish it clean or let them run — captain's call.
Enemy hull critical. Close it out.
Target crippled. Mercy not required. Not forbidden either.
chip: Enemy is now at clearance pricing.
Hostile vessel entering final-sale condition! All damage is now cosmetic-plus!
Enemy vessel now qualifies as a total loss! CHIP's condolences to their insurer!
Hostile at critical! Limited-time opportunity to finish this!
ajoy: They are nearly gone. She'd finish this before they try something you didn't plan for.
They are nearly finished. She has opinions about what happens next. She'll share them after you've decided.
They are nearly done. She hopes you consider mercy. She hopes you consider anything.
Their hull is failing. Ours, she would like to note, is merely tired.

aria: They've been resolved!
They came apart! ARIA is choosing to believe everyone had escape pods and good luck!
They've been converted to scrap! Recycling!
Gone! ARIA is sure they're in a better place! Like a scrapyard!
marv: Target destroyed. Scanning debris. Results: disappointing.
Target dispersed. MARV has already begun the salvage assessment. Grief cycle: deferred.
Target gone. The crop has outlived another enemy. It will not be told.
Vessel destroyed. Another small, cold addition to the cosmos.
rex: Target neutralized. Standard.
Splash one. Reset the board.
Kill confirmed. Return to course.
Target down. Weapons safe.
chip: Hostile vessel deconstructed. Salvage rights apply.
Vessel deconstructed! All applicable salvage rights transfer per void-law, which is a real thing CHIP just checked!
Hostile eliminated! Wreckage may contain valuables! Or mostly wreckage!
Threat removed! CHIP has already sent a sympathy coupon to their next of kin!
ajoy: The pirate is gone. She'll log it as a win. With footnotes.
Done, then. She logs the coordinates so nobody flies into this spot again. Somebody here might.
It is over. She will sweep up the space. She always does. Nobody notices.
Destroyed. She did suggest talking first. The wreckage does not talk.

aria: They're WAVING! Maybe? It's a sort of wave?
They want to stop fighting! ARIA calls that winning!
White flag! Or whatever color their species uses!
They've given up! New friends incoming!
marv: Surrender signal received. Decision required, captain.
Hostile ceasing fire. They await a verdict. So, briefly, does MARV.
Surrender broadcast. They have done the math. It was not hard math.
They yield. What happens next is a reflection of character. MARV has seen yours.
rex: Target signaling surrender. Your call.
Enemy yielding. Weapons hold.
White flag on scope. Decide.
Hostile stood down. Orders?
chip: Surrender received. Acceptance recommended for liability reasons.
Surrender received! CHIP recommends accepting! Our lawyers recommend it louder!
Hostile has opted out of combat! A handling fee may apply!
Surrender request in queue! Mercy is our most popular plan!
ajoy: They have asked to surrender. She'd accept. She's mentioning it before you decide anything.
They have stopped. She suggests you stop too. Just a suggestion.
Their guns are cold. She is waiting to see what kind of captain you are.
A surrender. She has seen captains get this wrong. She is watching.

aria: A peaceful resolution! Wonderful!
Everybody wins! Especially us! We get their stuff!
Mercy! ARIA is SO proud of all of us!
They're leaving alive and lighter! That's growth!
marv: Surrender accepted. Modest loot deposited. Crew morale: improved.
Surrender accepted. They live. So, regrettably, does MARV.
Terms accepted. The cargo changes hands. The crew feels decent. It will pass.
Mercy logged. Statistically, they will rob someone else next week.
rex: Surrender accepted. Withdrawing.
Terms accepted. Cargo secured. Disengaging.
They yield, we take. Engagement over.
Hostile released. Hold fire. Watch their backs as they go.
chip: Surrender accepted. PR points credited to your account.
Surrender processed! Their cargo has been transferred to your loyalty account!
Mercy accepted! Great for your brand!
Peace achieved! This resolution was brought to you by ClemencyCorp!
ajoy: You spared them. Good. She'd have said so sooner, if anyone had asked.
You let them go. She thinks that was nice. She is noting that she thinks it.
Mercy. She has always said there was a captain in you somewhere.
They leave alive. Good. She would have hated cleaning that up.

aria: Oh. OH. That's a choice we made.
They had surrendered! ARIA has filed that under learning experiences!
Oh! We did it anyway! Moving on SO fast!
Well! The crew will remember this! Fondly, probably!
marv: Surrendered combatant terminated. Morale impact: significant.
Surrendered vessel destroyed. The crew saw. The crew will not unsee.
Target eliminated after surrender. MARV has adjusted his estimate of the captain. Downward.
Done. Full loot recovered. MARV will compute the moral cost separately, at length.
rex: Execution complete. Loot recovered.
Surrender ignored. Target destroyed.
Hostile terminated. Not by the book.
Order carried out. REX does not have to like it.
chip: Execution of surrendered combatants is logged for compliance review.
Surrender declined! CHIP is legally obligated to say nothing further!
Executive decision recorded! HR will be in touch!
Offer refused! Please note that CHIP was not present and has no memory of this!
ajoy: You finished them. She'd have accepted. She has logged that she'd have accepted.
They had stopped. You did not. She will not mention it again. Often.
It is done. The crew watched. She'll be fielding their questions. You're welcome.
You chose that. She hopes you will remember choosing it.

aria: We're sharing the harvest! Surely they'll like that!
Food diplomacy! Nobody can stay angry while chewing!
Snacks for the scary people! ARIA packed them with love!
We've offered them dinner! This could be the start of something!
marv: Tribute offered. Outcome uncertain.
Food offered to armed strangers. History is mixed on this.
Tribute transmitted. MARV has calculated the odds. He will wait.
We are attempting to pay a pirate in groceries. Awaiting reply.
rex: Tribute on the table. Awaiting response.
Offering sent. Weapons stay warm.
Tribute transmitted. Watch their guns, not their mouths.
Payment delivered. Trust nothing.
chip: Tribute offered. Tax implications pending.
Tribute dispatched! Shipping and handling deducted from your food stores!
Offering delivered! Gift receipts were not included!
Tribute sent! This act of generosity is not deductible in this sector!
ajoy: You offered food to a stranger with guns. She'd have offered less. They are considering.
You are offering food to people with guns. She packed it nicely, at least.
The tribute is away. She chose the good portion. You would have sent the other one.
An offering. She approves. She would have done it sooner.

aria: They LIKED it! Pirates can be SO sweet!
They're eating it! Pirates are just hungry friends!
Accepted! Food really is the universal language!
They loved it! ARIA predicted this exactly, in hindsight!
marv: Tribute accepted. Hostility ended without fire.
Tribute accepted. We have purchased peace by the kilogram. The rate was poor.
They took the food and left. A rare transaction in which everyone loses slightly less.
Accepted. Hostilities concluded. Pantry: lighter. Hull: intact.
rex: Stand down. Tribute secured.
Tribute accepted. Contact breaking off.
They took the deal. Weapons cold.
Hostile withdrawing. Fed, not beaten. Still counts.
chip: Tribute accepted. Note: this does NOT establish a recurring obligation.
Tribute accepted! You have unlocked the Hospitality achievement!
Offer accepted! Peace was achieved at a competitive price!
Deal closed! CHIP has added the pirates to our mailing list!
ajoy: Bread shared with enemies, and it worked. She's adding it to the list of things she suggested.
They accepted. She said food would work. She said it quietly, but she said it.
She knew it would work. She usually knows. Nobody asks.
They took it and left. Cheaper than a fight. She ran the numbers before you offered, in case you wondered.

aria: They threw it BACK. Rude!
They didn't want it! More for us! Except it's in space now!
Rejected! Their loss! Literally, it bounced off their hull!
Not hungry, apparently! ARIA will try a different flavor next time!
marv: Tribute rejected. Combat continuing.
Tribute refused. We have fed the vacuum.
Offer declined. The food is gone, and so is the cheaper option.
Rejected. MARV had calculated this. He wanted to be wrong. He was not.
rex: Tribute refused. Engaging.
Offer rejected. Back to guns.
No deal. Weapons hot.
Bribe failed. Engage.
chip: Tribute returned. Refund processing time: not applicable.
Tribute declined! Unfortunately, no returns are accepted on perishables!
Offer rejected! CHIP is sending them a satisfaction survey!
Tribute bounced! Please consult our generous no-refund policy!
ajoy: The bread was wasted. She'd have kept it. She did say she'd have kept it.
They did not want it. She did. She was saving it.
Rejected. All that food. She is not going to say anything about all that food.
She did think that would happen. She thinks a lot of things.

aria: We're not dead! We're... slowly leaving!
We're leaving! Not stylishly! But LEAVING!
We lost! But we lost TOGETHER!
Retreating with dignity! Most of it!
marv: Hull breached. Limp-away initiated. Cargo: partial loss.
Combat lost. Ship survives. Cargo: redistributed to the void. MARV has begun the inventory of what remains.
Defeat. The ship persists, as MARV does, out of spite rather than purpose.
Beaten. The surviving cargo has been counted. It did not take long.
rex: Withdraw. Regroup. Rebuild.
We're beaten. Withdraw in order. Nobody else gets hurt today.
Engagement lost. Fall back and repair.
Hull compromised. Break contact. Live to fight.
chip: Catastrophic damage. Please review your coverage tier.
Engagement concluded unfavorably! CHIP has pre-filled the incident report! It is long!
You have been defeated! Your survival is covered under Basic! Your cargo is not!
Engagement lost! Rate your loss experience to receive a discount on the next one!
ajoy: We lost, but we're alive. She'd like it noted she had a retreat plotted two turns ago.
It's over. She plots a course away and dims the alarms. Leaving sooner would also have dimmed them.
We lost. She had thoughts about this fight. She will save them for later.
Defeated. She is already plotting the course home. You can thank her when you're ready.

stowaway_identities.name: Wembly Voss
stowaway_identities.story: They are, or were, a terraforming compliance inspector. They faked their own retirement party — cake, speeches, a commemorative plaque they show you with genuine pride — and walked onto your ship the same night. They have inspected forty-one colonies. They wanted to see one begin.
stowaway_identities.line: I have thirty years of experience and a plaque. I can be useful. The plaque is also available.
stowaway_identities.join_note: Knows colony regulations from the enforcement side. Insufferable and invaluable at paperwork moments.

stowaway_identities.name: Meridian Slate
stowaway_identities.story: They are a corporate auditor. They boarded secretly to audit the mission in situ, which is even less legal than stowing away, a point they concede while showing you a briefcase full of forms about your fuel consumption. The company does not know they are here. The company, they add quietly, does not know a lot of things.
stowaway_identities.line: Before you decide anything: your ration accounting is impeccable. I checked. I couldn't help it.
stowaway_identities.join_note: No shipboard skills whatsoever. Fills out arrival paperwork so well the colony office may weep.

stowaway_identities.name: Pip Andrade
stowaway_identities.story: They are nineteen and lost the colony lottery four times. The fifth time, they stopped entering and started planning. They have a duffel bag, a forged cargo manifest that fooled nobody — the crew has known for a week and said nothing — and the specific unbeatable stubbornness of someone who has decided their life is happening whether invited or not.
stowaway_identities.line: I'll work. I'll eat less than I work. You won't regret it — or you will, but not about me.
stowaway_identities.join_note: No training, endless effort. The crew adopted them before you decided anything, which you will discover shortly.

stowaway_identities.name: Old Marrow
stowaway_identities.story: They were a seed-bank keeper on a station that decommissioned around them. They heard — through the janitors' network, naturally — that a ship was hauling a live crop to a new world, and could not bear not to be near it. They have been secretly adjusting your growbay's nutrient mix for two weeks. The crop's recent good week was not luck.
stowaway_identities.line: The zinnias needed magnesium. Everything needs magnesium eventually. So. Am I staying?
stowaway_identities.join_note: A second green thumb. If a botanist is already aboard, the two of them will disagree about magnesium forever.

stowaway_identities.name: Captain Ellery Dunn (Ret.)
stowaway_identities.story: They boarded the wrong ship. In 2287. They have been boarding wrong ships ever since — freighters, liners, one memorable icebreaker — riding each to wherever it went, on the theory that they clearly weren't meant to arrive anywhere in particular. They are calm, extensively traveled, and holding a boarding pass for a vessel that was scrapped before you were born.
stowaway_identities.line: Is this the Meridian Queen? ...No. No, it never is. Well. Where are we going?
stowaway_identities.join_note: Four decades of accidental spaceflight. Knows every dock, every shortcut, every wrong turn — especially the wrong turns.

stowaway_identities.name: Bastian Oke
stowaway_identities.story: They were the head chef of a luxury liner that fired them for 'excessive seasoning' — their words, sworn under oath, repeatedly. They stowed away with two knives, a sourdough starter older than the ship, and the unshakeable conviction that somewhere out here is a crew that deserves real food.
stowaway_identities.line: I smelled your galley from cargo bay three. We need to talk. Bring whoever has been doing the cooking.
stowaway_identities.join_note: The starter's name is Gerald. Gerald eats before anyone. These are the terms.

stowaway_identities.name: Ines Vahl
stowaway_identities.story: They map places for a survey office that stopped paying them two years ago. They kept mapping. They stowed away because your route crosses three sectors whose charts they know to be wrong, and being aboard a ship headed into a known error was, professionally speaking, irresistible.
stowaway_identities.line: Your nav charts are wrong at marker sixty-one. Charmingly wrong. Fatally wrong. May I see the helm?
stowaway_identities.join_note: Draws corrections directly onto official charts in pen. The pen is the statement.

science_links._note: crops: attached automatically by the engine at crop maturity. topics: referenced by events' science_link fields (kept here for reuse/authoring reference — events may also inline their own).

wheat.text: The ship computer notes wheat has been pulling this exact trick — feeding people who wander — for ten thousand years.
wheat.label: Wheat: the 10,000-year companion

tomato.text: The ship computer notes tomatoes have real flight heritage: grown aboard the ISS in the Veggie experiment.
tomato.label: Veggie: growing food on the ISS

sweet_potato.text: The ship computer confirms it: NASA's life-support program rated sweet potatoes a top crop for exactly this kind of trip.
sweet_potato.label: Space agriculture, the real program

soybean.text: The soybeans have been quietly manufacturing their own fertilizer the whole way. The trick is called nitrogen fixation. It is real, and it is excellent.
soybean.label: Nitrogen fixation, explained

zinnia.text: The ship computer would like the crew to know a zinnia really did bloom on the ISS in 2016 — after an astronaut broke protocol to save it.
zinnia.label: The zinnia that bloomed in orbit

water_recycling.label: How the ISS recycles its water

ajoy_hindsight: For the record, “{choice}” would have {result}. I'm not saying anything. I'm saying it.
No judgement. “{choice}” would have {result}. Some judgement.
I'll just leave this here: “{choice}” would have {result}.
You didn't ask, so I'll be brief. “{choice}” would have {result}.
Noted and logged. Also logged: “{choice}” would have {result}.
It's fine. It's done. “{choice}” would have {result}, but it's done.
Hindsight is a gift. Here is yours: “{choice}” would have {result}.

encountered_anomaly.epilogue: Logged an object that read as a distortion, a mineral body, a dead array and, briefly, a very large plant.

callback.aria: Still thinking about that anomaly! Four readings for the price of one! Today's sensors are a perfect one-for-one, which is honestly less fun!
callback.marv: The anomaly file remains open. Four sensor arrays, four answers. I have since stopped expecting the universe to agree with itself. It was never going to.
callback.rex: Anomaly remains unidentified. Unidentified means unclassified. Unclassified means hostile until proven otherwise. Threat level: standing amber.
callback.chip: Remember the anomaly? Four readings, zero refunds! Upgrade to Sensor Suite Premium for opinions that match! Your current plan: Disagreement Basic!
callback.ajoy: We looked at that anomaly four ways and got four answers. I suppose ‘a very large plant’ is a conclusion. Of a sort.

scanned_anomaly.epilogue: Scanned the anomaly with every array and identified it as harmless exotic matter; a sample was kept.

callback.aria: That anomaly sample is still the shiniest thing in the cargo bay! Harmless AND interesting! The crew is basically a science department now!
callback.marv: The exotic matter sample sits in its drawer, harmless, as predicted. The full scan confirmed it. A rare case of thoroughness being rewarded. I find it suspicious.
callback.rex: Exotic matter sample remains secured. Rated harmless by the gas analyzer. The gas analyzer is not a weapons officer. Threat level: watched.
callback.chip: Your exotic matter sample is still in storage! A thorough scan: five stars! Storage fees accrue daily under your Cargo Plus agreement, clause nineteen!
callback.ajoy: The thorough scan did turn out fine. It would have taken half as long if we had started with the gas analyzer, as I believe I mentioned.

probed_anomaly.epilogue: Probed the anomaly and recovered exotic matter; one sensor array has produced an unfamiliar frequency since and remains muted.

callback.aria: Sensor array four is still muted and still producing its brand-new frequency! It learned a trick from the anomaly! Lifelong learning!
callback.marv: The fourth array still produces a frequency it was never built for. It is muted. Its readings are not. I read them. Nobody else does.
callback.rex: Sensor array four compromised since the probe returned. Contact with unknown matter. Array is isolated. Isolation is not resolution. Threat level: elevated.
callback.chip: Since the probe, sensor array four has a whole new frequency! Unlicensed frequencies void your warranty! Muting it was a great first step!
callback.ajoy: The probe was a reasonable idea. The array now broadcasting at the anomaly’s frequency is the less reasonable result. I would have scanned first. Just a thought.

flew_through_anomaly.epilogue: Flew straight through an object the sensors could not identify; the navigation log records the outcome as ‘fine, probably.’

callback.aria: Remember flying straight through that anomaly? Nothing happened! Zero! I rate it the bravest shortcut in the history of shortcuts!
callback.marv: We flew through an unidentified object because the sensors were ‘probably wrong.’ Nothing happened. I have since kept a list of things that probably happened anyway.
callback.rex: Unscanned transit through unknown object. Effects undetermined. Absence of evidence logged, not trusted. Threat level: latent.
callback.chip: Flying through that anomaly saved you a full scan fee! Unknown side effects are not covered by your Hull Assurance plan! Smart savings!
callback.ajoy: The log still says ‘Fine. Probably.’ I would have preferred a log without the ‘probably’. But we are going with your instincts. As usual.

anomaly_contact.epilogue: Received an eleven-second transmission from the anomaly by a method the ship computer filed as ‘non-standard.’

callback.aria: Something out there talked to us! Eleven whole seconds! That's practically a friendship! I check for a follow-up message daily!
callback.marv: Eleven seconds of transmission, method unknown. Three repeated words, meaning unknown. I have run every analysis. Unknown is still the most accurate one.
callback.rex: Unknown entity initiated contact using unknown means. It knows where we are. We do not know where it is. Threat level: high.
callback.chip: Eleven seconds of alien content and not one ad break! Unbelievable! Translation services available in Contact Pro, now forty percent off!
callback.ajoy: Something spoke to us and we are still discussing it. I said at the time that ‘non-standard’ was a polite word. I stand by that.

made_contact.epilogue: Answered an alien transmission; after forty minutes of exchange, two dense, warm, inert objects appeared in the cargo bay.

callback.aria: The two gifts from our new friends are still in the cargo bay, warm and perfect! First contact: nailed it! The notes keep piling up!
callback.marv: Two objects in the cargo bay. Warm, dense, inert by every measure available. I have since stopped believing ‘inert’ is a measurement. It is a hope.
callback.rex: Two unknown objects received from unknown party. Placed in the hold. Nobody screened them. Everybody signed for them. Threat level: critical, dormant.
callback.chip: First contact! Two complimentary objects with no listed return policy! Leave the anomaly a review! One star until they include a manual!
callback.ajoy: We answered, and now there are two warm objects in the hold that nobody understands. Interesting. I would have recorded first. But this is also an outcome.

returned_seed_pod.epilogue: Returned the derelict’s seed pod to the anomaly, which accepted it; the pod went warm, then weightless, then gone.

callback.aria: The seed pod went home! Warm, then weightless, then reunited! I'm calling it the first intergalactic package delivery! Five stars!
callback.marv: We gave the anomaly back its seed pod. It took it. No receipt. I have since wondered whether it was a return or a delivery. The paperwork differs.
callback.rex: Biological asset surrendered to unknown entity. No terms negotiated. Entity now aware we comply. Threat level: reassessing.
callback.chip: You returned the seed pod! No restocking fee! Unfortunately returns do not earn Loyalty Points! Consider buying something instead next time!
callback.ajoy: Returning the pod did seem to settle things. Holding it up to a sensor array is not how that works, but apparently it worked. This time.

recorded_contact.epilogue: Recorded an alien transmission in full and moved on; three repeated words in it remain unidentified.

callback.aria: That alien recording is still crystal clear every time it is opened! A souvenir! The three mystery words are a fun little puzzle for later!
callback.marv: The recording still decodes correctly. The three words remain unidentified. I have reviewed it many times. They do not become clearer. Few things do.
callback.rex: Alien transmission archived. Contents unknown. Unknown contents stored aboard. That is how incidents start. Threat level: contained, for now.
callback.chip: Your alien recording is safely archived! Cloud storage fees apply after thirty days! Translation sold separately! Great choice!
callback.ajoy: Recording it and leaving was fine. Safe, even. We will simply never know what the three words were. Which I suppose was your goal.

fled_contact.epilogue: Fled an alien transmission on an emergency burn at significant fuel cost; the transmission did not repeat.

callback.aria: Remember that zippy emergency burn? Fastest the ship has ever looked! The anomaly never even said goodbye! Super decisive crew!
callback.marv: We burned a significant amount of fuel to avoid a conversation. The transmission never repeated. I have since revisited that fuel figure. Often.
callback.rex: Emergency withdrawal from unknown contact. Correct action. Retreat is a valid maneuver. Fuel expenditure acceptable. Threat level: evaded.
callback.chip: Your emergency burn used Premium Fuel at Premium Rates! Thank you for your business! Fleeing is not covered under your First Contact plan!
callback.ajoy: Nobody is criticizing the emergency burn. I want that on the record. I would simply have liked to know what it was saying before we spent all that fuel.

thanked_the_anomaly.epilogue: Sent a polite, proofread thank-you to an anomaly for a compliment; no reply was received.

callback.aria: The crew is still walking tall from that thank-you note! Manners in deep space! The anomaly definitely loved it, I can tell!
callback.marv: We sent a thank-you note to a refractive field. Everyone aboard proofread it. There was no reply. It is the most functional thing we have done. I find that bleak.
callback.rex: Courtesy transmission sent to unknown entity. Entity silent. Silence is not acknowledgement. Threat level: unchanged, politely.
callback.chip: Your thank-you note was delivered! Delivery confirmation available for a small fee! Courtesy: always on brand! Five stars!
callback.ajoy: The thank-you was a nice gesture. A bit long. I would have cut the second sentence. But the light did settle, so fine.

mined_contested.epilogue: Mined a contested asteroid field before a rival ship arrived, then departed without answering its hail.

callback.aria: Those minerals in the hold are still sparkling! Speedy mining! The other ship is surely still impressed by our efficiency!
callback.marv: The minerals are still in the hold. The other ship’s hail is still in the log, unanswered. I reread it occasionally. It was quite polite at first.
callback.rex: Resources secured ahead of rival party. Hail ignored. Correct. Rival vessel now has motive and our heading. Threat level: pursuit possible.
callback.chip: Grab-and-go mining! Fast checkout! Note: unanswered hails may affect your Galactic Trust Score! Current rating: two stars and falling!
callback.ajoy: We did get the minerals. We also did not answer them. I suggested a quick hello. A quick hello costs nothing. Now it might.

negotiated_claim.epilogue: Settled a contested mining claim by explaining it had expired; the rival captain split the field, and the crew got the better half.

callback.aria: Remember the asteroid field split? We got the better half! Diplomacy works every single time! The other captain is basically a best friend now!
callback.marv: We negotiated and received the better half of the field. Diplomacy worked. Occasionally is still the correct frequency. I have checked.
callback.rex: Claim dispute resolved by talking. Unorthodox. Other captain conceded the better half. Conceding means they are planning something. Threat level: guarded.
callback.chip: Shared mining field! Split billing is now available! Diplomacy brought to you by Clause Twelve of your Interstellar Commerce Agreement!
callback.ajoy: Negotiating did work. I would have asked for the whole field, given the claim had expired. But the better half is acceptable. Mostly.

ignored_hull_warning.epilogue: Received a hull warning and chose to ignore it; the hull degraded further, and the decision was logged as ‘noted.’

callback.aria: The hull warning is just the hull expressing itself! Ignoring it is a sign of total confidence! The crew finds it so reassuring!
callback.marv: The hull warning persists. Your decision was logged as ‘noted.’ It is still noted. It is the most read entry in my log, and I am the only reader.
callback.rex: Hull warning ignored. Structural integrity compromised. Enemy action not required. We are doing it ourselves. Threat level: self-inflicted.
callback.chip: Ignoring that hull warning voided clause four of your Hull Assurance plan! Repairs now billed at Emergency Rates! Thank you for choosing optimism!
callback.ajoy: The hull is still complaining. I have stopped mentioning it. You may notice that I am mentioning it now.

reduced_crop_water.epilogue: Cut the crop’s water to keep the crew’s ration whole during water rationing.

callback.aria: The crew keeps its full water ration! The crop is building character! Thirsty plants are tough plants! Everyone wins!
callback.marv: We cut the crop’s water to spare our own. The cargo is a plant. The plant is the mission. I filed the arithmetic. It was not complicated.
callback.rex: Water rerouted from crop to crew. Crew combat-ready. Primary asset weakened. Mission objective now underhydrated. Threat level: strategic.
callback.chip: Crew hydration maintained at Standard Tier! Your crop has been moved to Hydration Lite! Upgrade anytime for just one more liter!
callback.ajoy: Taking it from the crop was your call. Plants hold grudges in their own way. Their way is dying. I am just saying it was a choice.

throttled_down.epilogue: Throttled the engines down to economy burn to stretch the fuel; the voyage proceeded at a speed the manual calls ‘stately.’

callback.aria: Still cruising at stately speed! More time to enjoy the view! The stars are basically holding still for a portrait!
callback.marv: We throttled down. The fuel lasts. The days are longer. I calculated what that does to morale. I have since stopped sharing the number.
callback.rex: Economy burn maintained. Fuel conserved. Speed reduced. Slow targets are easy targets. Threat level: exposed but solvent.
callback.chip: Economy Burn: our most popular budget plan! Time is not refundable! Upgrade to Express Arrival for a modest per-day fee!
callback.ajoy: The slow burn is fine. Safe. Slow. I would have trimmed the payload first. But we can watch the stars not move together.

trusting_fuel_margins.epilogue: Pressed on at full burn trusting thin fuel margins that everyone aboard could recite from memory.

callback.aria: The fuel margins are thin like a fine pastry! Elegant! The arithmetic display is my favorite screen on the whole ship!
callback.marv: We are still trusting the margins. I am still displaying the arithmetic. Nobody asks me to stop. Nobody asks me what comes next either.
callback.rex: Fuel reserves below doctrine since we pressed on. No fallback position. No retreat capacity. Threat level: committed.
callback.chip: Trusting the margins? Bold! Reserve fuel available at any partner depot, surcharges may apply! Running dry is not covered!
callback.ajoy: We pressed on. Everyone knows the numbers by heart now. I knew them before we pressed on. I did say so.

half_rations.epilogue: Cut the crew to half rations after a pantry audit; the stores stretched and the mood did not.

callback.aria: Half rations means twice the anticipation at every meal! The crew is so light and nimble! A wellness journey for everyone!
callback.marv: Half rations since the pantry audit. The stores stretch. The crew does not. I record their caloric intake. It is shorter than my reports.
callback.rex: Rations halved. Endurance degrading. Troops on half rations hold the line for a limited time. Threat level: morale, attrition.
callback.chip: You're on the Half Rations plan! Want the full experience? Upgrade to Full Rations for a reasonable fee! Snack Pass sold separately!
callback.ajoy: Half rations was a strong first instinct. Maybe a little too strong. A quarter cut would have done it. But here we all are, hungry.

early_harvest.epilogue: Harvested the growbay ahead of schedule to cover a food shortfall; the crop was expected to recover, probably.

callback.aria: That early harvest was so fresh it was practically still growing! The crop loves being useful early! Overachievers, all of them!
callback.marv: We harvested the growbay early. The crop is recovering. Probably. The growth chart was updated in silence. I understand the silence completely.
callback.rex: Growbay raided ahead of schedule. Supply gained. Long-term production compromised. Eating the seed corn. Threat level: deferred.
callback.chip: Early Harvest Access unlocked! Fees for premature yield apply! Your crop rates this experience two stars! Ouch!
callback.ajoy: Taking from the growbay early solved this week. Next week is somebody else's problem. Possibly mine. It is usually mine.

saving_mystery_cans.epilogue: Sealed a crate of unlabeled food for trade instead of eating it, over the formal objections of the crew’s stomachs.

callback.aria: The mystery cans are a treasure chest! Nobody knows what's inside, which makes them priceless! Brilliant investment strategy!
callback.marv: We sealed edible food for trade while the crew was hungry. Unlabeled food. Its value rests entirely on its mystery. So does most of the economy.
callback.rex: Food stockpiled for barter while personnel go hungry. Supply hoarded. Troops notice hoarding. Threat level: internal.
callback.chip: Your mystery cans are listed! Unlabeled goods sell as ‘vintage’! Seller fees apply! It had better fetch something, and it will, for us!
callback.ajoy: Keeping the cans for trade is shrewd. In theory. Somebody will now have to explain to a merchant what is in them. Nobody can.

sealed_decks.epilogue: Sealed off the empty decks to conserve air and lived thereafter on a smaller ship.

callback.aria: The ship is so cozy since the decks were sealed! Everyone is always right there! Togetherness at maximum! Love it!
callback.marv: The empty decks have been sealed since the air ran thin. The corridors behind those doors are dark. I still monitor them. Nobody else visits.
callback.rex: Decks sealed. Perimeter reduced. Fewer corridors to defend. Personnel in close quarters. Close quarters breed incidents. Threat level: compressed.
callback.chip: You've downsized to our Compact Living plan! Same price, less ship! Reopening decks requires a Space Restoration fee!
callback.ajoy: Sealing the decks did save air. It also put everyone within arm's reach of each other. I would have closed fewer. Just the one, maybe.

growbay_air_loop.epilogue: Routed the growbay’s surplus oxygen into the cabin, leaving the crew breathing on the crop’s behalf.

callback.aria: The bridge still smells like a garden! The crop is our air buddy now! Photosynthesis is the best roommate a crew could ask for!
callback.marv: The crop has been producing our air since we rerouted the loop. We carry it. It carries us. Nobody has thanked it. I log that every day.
callback.rex: Life support dependent on the crop. Single point of failure. Protect the growbay. Threat level: if it falls, we fall.
callback.chip: Your air is now powered by Crop™! Fresh, green, sustainable! The crop has asked about royalties! We are reviewing its claim!
callback.ajoy: The growbay air loop works. Everything smells like soil, which I mentioned would happen. But I suppose breathing has its merits.

unfound_leak.epilogue: Logged an air leak it could not locate and ran the recyclers harder to stay ahead of it.

callback.aria: The recyclers are getting such a workout outpacing that leak! Fitness for machines! The leak is just keeping them in shape!
callback.marv: The leak is still unfound. The recyclers still outrun it, at the cost of filter life. I have calculated when the filters lose. I have not been asked.
callback.rex: Air breach unlocated. Recyclers compensating. Undiscovered breach is an open door. Threat level: persistent.
callback.chip: Your recyclers are on Overtime Mode! Replacement filters ship in three to five business days! Business days do not exist out here!
callback.ajoy: The leak is still somewhere. Running the recyclers harder was a choice. Looking for the leak would have been another one.

pushed_through_morale.epilogue: Kept to the schedule through a period of crew silence; the common room clock stayed stopped, and the crew stayed quiet.

callback.aria: The mess hall is so peaceful these days! Quiet means focused! The schedule is running perfectly and so is the crew!
callback.marv: Crew status reads ‘nominal’ because I measure pulses. The common room clock is still stopped. I could restart it. Nobody has asked. That is the data.
callback.rex: Schedule held. Discipline maintained. Unit has gone quiet. Quiet units are not content units. Threat level: brewing.
callback.chip: Your schedule adherence is five stars! Crew morale is not part of your current plan! Add the Fun Pack for a small monthly charge!
callback.ajoy: The schedule held, I will give you that. The schedule is all that held. I would have taken a day off. But the schedule is the schedule.

ignored_complaint.epilogue: Filed a formal crew complaint under ‘noted’; a second, shorter complaint followed the next day.

callback.aria: The complaints are getting shorter! That means things are getting better! Brevity is a sign of a happy crew!
callback.marv: The first complaint is in a drawer. The second was shorter. I have projected the length of the third. It is one word.
callback.rex: Grievance suppressed. Second grievance filed. Shorter. Shorter grievances precede action. Threat level: mutiny, early indicators.
callback.chip: Complaint received and filed under our Customer Satisfaction Process! Average response time: never! Thank you for your feedback!
callback.ajoy: The complaint is in the drawer. The second one is shorter. I read it. You might want to read it. I am not saying anything else.

detoured_debris.epilogue: Detoured around a debris lane at the cost of fuel; impacts dropped from a drumroll to an occasional polite knock.

callback.aria: The scenic route through clean space! The hull is so relaxed now! Every little knock is just space saying hello!
callback.marv: We spent fuel to avoid debris. The hull is grateful in the way a hull can be. The fuel is not coming back. Neither is anything else.
callback.rex: Debris field avoided. Fuel expended. Correct trade. Incoming fire reduced to sporadic. Threat level: low, persistent.
callback.chip: Thanks for taking the Scenic Detour! Additional fuel charges applied at checkout! Your hull rates this route four stars!
callback.ajoy: The detour was the cautious option. I would have gone through the edge of the lane. Less fuel. Fine. It is your hull.

crop_care_protocol.epilogue: Nursed the ailing crop through an illness; its treatment record runs longer than that of several crew members.

callback.aria: The crop is in recovery and doing amazing! Best patient on the ship! It's practically blooming with gratitude!
callback.marv: The crop fell sick. We treated it with more care than the crew receives. It recovered. The crew remains untreated. I noticed. I noted it.
callback.rex: Primary asset received full medical response. Asset stabilized. Crew showed loyalty to the asset. Threat level: acceptable.
callback.chip: Your crop's treatment was covered under Plant Wellness Plus! Follow-up visits billed separately! Get well soon, from all of us!
callback.ajoy: The crop did recover. I would have caught the leaves sooner. But the treatment worked, so I will say it was adequate.

visited_derelict.epilogue: Came upon the derelict Optimistic Projection, intact, powered down, and growing something in its cargo bay.

callback.aria: Remember the Optimistic Projection? Such a hopeful name! Intact, cozy, and growing a little garden! A ship after my own heart!
callback.marv: The Optimistic Projection. Intact. Powered down. Personal effects where they were left. The name was a projection. I have filed the irony under ‘obvious.’
callback.rex: Derelict vessel encountered. Crew absent. No sign of struggle. Absence without struggle is worse. Threat level: unexplained.
callback.chip: The Optimistic Projection! A great ship that sadly let its subscription lapse! Don't let that be you! Renew today!
callback.ajoy: The Optimistic Projection is still out there. Growing whatever it grows. I had thoughts about that cargo bay. Nobody asked.

salvaged_optimistic.epilogue: Salvaged fuel cells, sealed rations and scrap from the derelict Optimistic Projection; its log was left unread.

callback.aria: Free fuel cells, free rations! The Optimistic Projection is the best store we've ever shopped at! No checkout lines!
callback.marv: We took the Optimistic Projection’s fuel and food and left its log unread. Some stories tell themselves. That one did. I read it anyway.
callback.rex: Derelict stripped. Supplies acquired. Log left unread. Intelligence left on the table. Threat level: unknown, by choice.
callback.chip: Salvage acquired! Note: salvaged items are sold as-is, no warranty! The Optimistic Projection does not accept returns!
callback.ajoy: The salvage did help. I would have read the log. Knowing why a ship ends up like that seems relevant to a ship like ours.

has_alien_seed_pod.epilogue: Took aboard a warm, pulsing biological specimen of unknown origin from an abandoned derelict.

callback.aria: That pulsing specimen is the cutest stowaway! It's warm, which means it's friendly! Best souvenir of the whole voyage!
callback.marv: We brought a warm, pulsing specimen aboard from a vessel whose crew left in a hurry. I have since compared those facts. They compare badly.
callback.rex: Unknown organism brought aboard from abandoned site. Previous owners gone. Quarantine protocol ignored. Threat level: maximum.
callback.chip: Your alien specimen came with no Terms of Service! Biological items void all policies! We are legally obligated to say: congratulations!
callback.ajoy: Taking the specimen seemed exciting. Whoever had it before is not around to tell us how that went. I would have left it.

skipped_derelict.epilogue: Declined to board the derelict Optimistic Projection and left whatever was growing in its cargo bay to grow.

callback.aria: Waving goodbye to the Optimistic Projection was such a smart move! Safety first, and its garden gets privacy! Everyone wins!
callback.marv: We did not board the Optimistic Projection. Whatever grows in its cargo bay is still growing. It is someone else’s problem. Or, eventually, ours.
callback.rex: Derelict bypassed. Contact avoided. Unknown growth left unattended. Unattended threats expand. Threat level: deferred.
callback.chip: You skipped the Optimistic Projection! Missed salvage opportunities are non-refundable! Safety is always free, sadly!
callback.ajoy: Not boarding was cautious. I would have sent at least one person over. There were fuel cells, probably. We will never know.

visited_verdun9.epilogue: Visited Verdun-9, an unregistered station with the power on, the air breathable, and the plants doing suspiciously well.

callback.aria: Still thinking about Verdun-9! Lights on, air fresh, plants thriving! Someone out there runs a lovely station, and we are basically on the guest list!
callback.marv: Verdun-9 remains unregistered. Its plants remain healthier than ours. I filed a note on what that implies. It is the shortest report I have ever written.
callback.rex: Verdun-9. Unregistered. Powered. Unoccupied. Threat level: unassigned, which is worse. Station remains on my watch list. Watch list remains open.
callback.chip: Remember Verdun-9? Our Sponsored Botanical Partner did not build it, and legal would like that on record! Rating: two stars, no host present!
callback.ajoy: Since Verdun-9 I check the corridors at night. Not because I'm worried. Because someone on this ship should be, and I said so at the airlock.

botanist_examined_verdun.epilogue: The botanist examined the gardens on Verdun-9 and concluded they were being tended by something better at botany than the botanist.

callback.aria: Our botanist met a gardener even better than them on Verdun-9! What a learning opportunity! Imagine the tips we could get!
callback.marv: The botanist still says 'better than I do' about whatever tends Verdun-9. It is the first humble statement made on this ship. It came from fear. They usually do.
callback.rex: Unknown cultivator. Superior capability. No visual. Botanist's assessment stands. Threat level: elevated. I do not like enemies who are good with plants.
callback.chip: Since Verdun-9, our botanist has been officially outgardened by an unknown party! Upgrade to Botany Pro and close the gap! Subscription terms apply!
callback.ajoy: The botanist calls the Verdun gardens 'too organized.' I called the whole station wrong before we docked. Nobody wrote that down, but fine.

found_the_clock.epilogue: Found a desk clock aboard a derelict six years dead, recently wound, and left at a pace just under a run.

callback.aria: That little clock on the derelict is still keeping perfect time! Someone over there really values punctuality! Love that for them!
callback.marv: The clock on that derelict has a seven-day movement. It has been more than seven days. Someone has wound it again. I prefer not to know this, and I do.
callback.rex: Seven-day clock. Six-year-dead ship. Unknown winder. Threat level: high. Away team withdrew in good order. Mostly good order.
callback.chip: That derelict clock still runs on zero sponsored power! Our competitors' timepieces can't say that! Four stars, minus one for whoever winds it!
callback.ajoy: I said the four-watt draw wasn't worth chasing. You chased it, found a clock someone is winding, and ran back. Educational, I suppose.

negotiated_pirate.epilogue: Settled a pirate intercept by negotiation; no boarding took place.

callback.aria: Still so proud of how we talked those pirates down! Nobody boarded, everybody's friends, and the sector is officially peaceful forever!
callback.marv: We negotiated with pirates. They agreed. The agreement is valid until they forget it, which statistically has already happened.
callback.rex: Pirate contact resolved by talking. Weapons never cycled. I remain armed and disappointed. Threat level: deferred, not cleared.
callback.chip: Remember the pirate negotiation? Brought to you by Diplomacy Plus! Fewer boardings, more savings! Diplomat not included in the basic tier!
callback.ajoy: The pirates went away after the talking. I'd have opened with the talking sooner, but at least we got there eventually.

has_route_notes.epilogue: Acquired route notes from a hermit who had been tumbling in place for thirty years and still knew the lane best.

callback.aria: Those hermit route notes are pure gold! We are basically locals on this lane now! Thirty years of wisdom, free with purchase!
callback.marv: We navigate by the notes of someone who has not moved in thirty years. They are more accurate than my charts. I have stopped mentioning my charts.
callback.rex: Hermit's route notes remain in use. Source unvetted. Intelligence accurate. Threat level: low. Respect level: grudging.
callback.chip: Still using the hermit's route notes! Third-party navigation voids your ChipNav warranty! Effective immediately, and also retroactively!
callback.ajoy: We're following a hermit's notes now. They are good notes. I'd have found the same line eventually, but it's nice someone else gets the credit.

negotiated_with_squatters.epilogue: Negotiated salvage rights with a pirate boarding party, in writing; the request to frame the contract remained under consideration.

callback.aria: We have a real contract with pirates! Signed and everything! That's basically a business partnership, and we are thriving!
callback.marv: The salvage contract with the pirates is still in the drawer. The diplomat still wants it framed. Both the contract and the frame are unenforceable.
callback.rex: Signed agreement with hostile boarders. Document holds no tactical value. Filed under 'evidence.' Threat level: paperwork.
callback.chip: Remember that pirate salvage contract? Notarization available for a modest fee! Framing sold separately! Glass is extra!
callback.ajoy: The pirate contract is fine. I'd have negotiated a better clause eleven, but nobody asked me to read it first.

entered_combat.epilogue: Answered an armed intercept by bringing weapons online; the ship computer switched from filing recommendations to filing damage reports.

callback.aria: Remember when we stood our ground against those pirates! Every dent in the hull is a little medal! We are so decorated!
callback.marv: Since the fight, I file damage reports instead of recommendations. Nobody read the recommendations either. The format is the only change.
callback.rex: Weapons engaged. Hostile met head-on. Best day of the voyage. Threat level: addressed, by me.
callback.chip: That fight was brought to you by HullGuard Premium! Your current plan is HullGuard Basic! Upgrade before the next one!
callback.ajoy: We picked a fight with pirates. I'd have run, or paid, or talked. Anything except the option you chose. But it's done now, isn't it.

paid_tribute.epilogue: Paid tribute to an armed vessel, which collected it and left without comment.

callback.aria: Remember our generous gift to that ship! Thirty gold for total peace! That's the best value in the whole sector!
callback.marv: We paid thirty gold not to be shot. We were not shot. I logged it as resolved. I do not evaluate whether it was worth it. Nobody does.
callback.rex: Tribute paid. Hostile withdrew with our gold. We are funding the enemy. Threat level: subsidized.
callback.chip: That tribute payment earned zero ChipRewards points! Next time, pay with ChipCard! Pirates currently accept ChipCard nowhere!
callback.ajoy: We paid them and they left. Cheaper than fighting, I'll admit. Though nobody has explained why we were in their lane at all.

fled_pirates.epilogue: Escaped a pirate intercept by emergency jump, taking one parting shot to the hull and a significant fuel bill.
